- **C++ deleted.** EEUnitClass.cpp -220, EEUnit.h -11, EECombatGoals.cpp +116 (the operations, the moved CBAD
  capture, the trample's entry), EECombatGoals.h +7, EEPhysicsModel.cpp +1: 237 deleted, 130 added, net -107.
- **Only a combat tour shows:** nothing new is drawn, but the volcano projectile's effect and the hit's
  `UnitDamaged` reaction (sounds, effects) now go through operations; EE-SIM and the captures run them without a
  window.
- **Not moved.** `LaunchShot`/`LaunchFromTurret`: object work only (create the shot, its goal, owner, location,
  cargo); an operation host would restate it line for line.
- **The shots' store records** (proposal for the core lane, RUST_PLAN's R5b.2 row): a table of unlisted units keyed
  by object, filled where `CreateUnit` returns a unit it did not insert, dropped in the destructor, the write-through
  falling back to it for id 0xffffffff.

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 10 (ServerRequestOp's exchange on the Rust op base; GetCertOp and DetectFirewallOp on it)

Branch `rust-won-net10`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 9. Nothing in the game reaches this code but
an Internet login (the lobby's version check, add friend, lost password and user name, the certificate request,
the firewall test, the directory and account ops; the servers are gone): only the drivers and the Rust replays
exercise it. RustServerOp::HostCall's new cases only compile; no tour, LAN game or EE-SIM run calls them.

- **The exchange is a Plan.** `reqhost.rs`'s `ReqPlan` keeps ServerRequestOp's members (the address list and its
  iterator, the current address, both sessions, the socket, the server context, the flags, the last server error,
  the certificate status, the request and the reply) and runs server.rs's exchange over a `RequestEnv` made of host
  calls (14 new codes: the auth type and context, ConnectTime, GetTimeout, the certificate's user id, the context's
  CopyAddresses and NotifyFailed, Get/PutSession, the crypt transform, the tracker's KillAll, the peer auth op's
  session and certificate status, the is-a-RecvMsgOp test). A derived op is a `HostRequest` behind a lock of its own
  (its steps may make host calls; the exchange's members stay behind the base's lock, never held across a call).
  What can call back into the op (Finish, Track with RunAsync of the firewall's datagram receive) runs after the
  derived op's lock is let go (`Own`, `HostRequest::datagram`).
- **Four kinds of derived op.** The round 7/8 Rust ops through `Plain` (the lobby's four now `RustServerOp::NewRequest`);
  GetCertOp (`certhost.rs`) and DetectFirewallOp (`fwhost.rs`): round 6's Rust objects, each statement of their old
  hook tables one host call (33 codes) and their own side (request, reply, server error, mode, time left, the session
  key) the exchange's; and the ops still derived in C++ (`CppReq`: the directory, account and routing request ops),
  whose GetNextRequest, CheckResponse and Reset are the C++ virtuals reached by three codes. ServerRequestOp is now a
  20-line `RustServerOp` those C++ ops build on (mRequest, mResponse, SetLastServerError, InvalidReplyHeader);
  ServerRequestOp.cpp, GetCertOp.cpp and DetectFirewallOp.cpp are deleted; GetCertOp and DetectFirewallOp are thin
  RustServerOps (constructor and the accessors the game uses).
- **Golden first, from ServerRequestOp.cpp as it was.** `won_hostop_test`'s new op `R`: the original half is
  ServerRequestOp.cpp's statements (server.rs's exchange over its members, its primitives as host calls over the
  stand-in), with a contest call, a ping and a user id lookup as the derived ops; 60 sequences appended to
  `golden_hostop.txt` (the earlier part byte for byte), the stand-in's answers biased for these sequences only
  (expired-session replies, ping and DB proxy replies, a peer auth certificate failure). 2,280,335 checks of 20,000
  sequences per op, 0 failed; a mutation (no PutSession, no server error for an invalid header) failed 66,489 and the
  Rust replay. GetCertOp and DetectFirewallOp: `golden_getcert.txt` and `golden_fwop.txt` replayed again through the
  base (every object statement a host call answered by the replays' stand-ins, the op's side the stand-in's);
  mutations (Verify's block and certificate swapped, the datagram host test inverted) fail them.
- **The original's undefined corners, defined.** The address iterator before any RunHook (default-constructed) and
  after the context's copy (left dangling: an empty copy finishes before the rewind, and a later callback read it;
  the driver crashed there before this was defined) is the list's begin; decrementing it at the begin gives the end,
  as a list's iterator does (an expired-session reply on a finished op). The reuse and expiry flags, unset before a
  RunHook, start false. A request's reply not received reads as NULL.
- **Two locks in one expression deadlock.** `assert_eq!((h.st().a, h.st().b), ..)` holds the first guard while taking
  the second: a test hung until it was split. Read the members under one guard.
- **`rust_build.py header` and `xtask cbindgen` disagreed once** on the order of two consts (the gate's header test
  failed after `header` said current): regenerate with `cargo run -p xtask -- cbindgen`.
- **Behaviour changes.** None intended. GetCertOp's GetErrorList, GetCommunityStatusList, GetSessionKey,
  SetNewPassword and SetAuthContext had no C++ caller and are now numbers of the Rust op only. RoutingLogic's
  `GetAddr()` on the group list op reads the first address from Rust.
- **Not moved, and why.** The ops still derived in C++ (GetDirOp, GetMultiDirOp, FindEntityOp, GetAliasDirOp,
  GetServiceOp, the account ops, the routing group list op) keep their C++ members because the lobby, EEWonNet and
  ServerContext read their DirEntity lists, GetEntityRequests and profiles: as Rust ops they need those readers on
  accessors first. HTTPGetOp / GetHTTPDocumentOp: not started (a scripted-socket driver the size of FTPGetOp's).

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 11 (the directory and account request ops as Rust ops; their readers on accessors)

Branch `rust-won-net11`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 10. Nothing in the game reaches these ops but
an Internet login (the lobby's room list and server query, EEWonNet's Titan list and account form, the patch ops'
listings, GameSpy's service lookup; the servers are gone): only the driver and the Rust replay exercise them. The
readers' new lines only compile; no tour, LAN game or EE-SIM run calls them.

- **What moved.** GetDirOp, GetMultiDirOp, GetAliasDirOp, FindEntityOp, GetServiceOp (with GetEntityRequest) and
  GetAccountOp, UpdateAccountOp are `RequestOp`s (`reqdir.rs`), made by `ee_won_reqops_new` (kinds 7 to 13, the
  members in a fixed order) and run by a `RustServerOp` through `Plain`. Their GetNextRequest, CheckResponse and
  Reset are the deleted classes' statements over `dirops.rs`, `dir.rs` and `db.rs`, which were Rust already.
- **Results are Rust lists, read through accessors.** The readers held references into the C++ ops (`const
  DirEntityList&`, `GetRequestList()`, `mProfileData`, `mEmail`). Now `RustServerOp::GetEntities(which, index)`
  makes a `DirEntityList` of what the Rust op holds (`ee_won_hostop_entities`: the list copied under the op's
  locks, then each entity handed to `DirEntityReplyParser::TakeEntity` outside them); `GetNum` and `GetBytes` read
  a query's status, the list count, the email, a newsletter. A by-value list read twice is two lists: each reader
  keeps one copy (EEWonNet's loop read `GetDirEntityList()` for its begin and its end).
- **Setters after the op was made.** RequestOp gained `set` (through the base's lock of the derived op), `num_at`
  (an element) and `entities`; Plan, HostRequest and the C ABI carry them. EEWonNet sets the newsletter of a running
  GetAccountOp after `RunAsync`, as the original did: the setter now waits for the op's lock instead of racing the
  request it builds.
- **Golden first.** `tests/won/won_reqdir_test.cpp`'s original half is the seven classes' statements and
  GetEntityRequest's over stand-ins (the parsers' statements over `dir.rs`, the requests through `won_dir_msg.h`
  and WONDBMsg.h); 1000 sequences printed to `golden_reqdir.txt` before the port (the request, up to six replies
  with headers right and wrong, statuses, sequence bytes, cut and mutated replies; a Reset and the next server's
  request at times). `reqdir::tests::golden` replays it; the driver checks 40,000 sequences (158,623 checks) against
  the Rust ops, 0 failed. A mutation (the failure count cleared by Reset, the find's service taken for a directory
  search) fails the replay. A first recording missed two members of each generated query (the replay caught it at
  the first request): print the members from the same statements that set them.
- **The original's undefined corners, defined.** A query's status before its first reply (its constructor left it
  unset) is `WS_None`. GetVersionOp read the first entity of an empty listing (past the list's end): an empty
  listing now gives no version. The ACLs' signed and unsigned conversions of the two parsers give the same bits
  in the members, so one entity maker serves both.
- **Deleted.** GetDirOp.cpp, GetMultiDirOp.cpp, GetAliasDirOp.cpp, FindEntityOp.cpp, GetServiceOp.cpp,
  GetEntityRequest.cpp, GetAccountOp.cpp, UpdateAccountOp.cpp, WONDirAlias.h, the classes in WONRouting.h and
  WONDirExtended.h, DirEntityReplyParser's parsers (their statements are `won_dir_test`'s original half now);
  WONDirRequest.h moved to `tests/won/won_dir_msg.h`. src+include: 175 lines added, 1,161 deleted.
  `GetEntityRequest::GetDirEntityMap` had no caller and went with its class (`dirops::group_keys` keeps the rule).
- **`rust_build.py header` and the gate's check.** `header` printed xtask's "N headers are current" after writing,
  whatever the gate's `cbindgen --check` then found. It now runs that same check (one command in both) after
  writing and fails when it disagrees. The round 10 case (a const order) did not reproduce in eight runs from both
  directories; cbindgen's crate order follows Cargo.lock and its constants their parse order, so a stale source
  read (a header written while sources changed) is the likelier cause.
- **The oracle on a rebuilt tree.** The shared open tree was rebuilt with main's Lua AIs mid-round: `compare ref`
  then differs at line 0 (the AI manifest's line) while every later line is identical. Compare the traces past
  that line before calling it a divergence.
- **Not moved, and why.** CreateAccountOp (its ElGamal public key and Blowfish session key are C++ objects;
  random keys need a seeded generator for a golden) and RoutingGetGroupListReqOp (its result is a C++ group map
  built by `WONRoutingMsg.h`'s records, read by `LobbyServer::SyncGroups`) still derive from the 20-line
  ServerRequestOp, which stays until they move. HTTPGetOp / GetHTTPDocumentOp: not started (HTTPEngine drives
  HTTPGetOp's sockets and modes; a scripted-socket driver the size of FTPGetOp's first).

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 12 (the last C++ request ops, HTTPGetOp and GetHTTPDocumentOp as Rust ops)

Branch `rust-won-net12`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 11. Nothing in the game reaches this code but
an Internet login (the lobby's create account form, its server room counts, the message of the day, terms of use
and advert downloads, EEWonNet's dead MOTD request; the WON servers are gone): only the drivers and the Rust
replays exercise it. RustServerOp::HostCall's new cases and the readers' new lines only compile; no tour, LAN game
or EE-SIM run calls them.

- **The last C++ request ops.** CreateAccountOp and RoutingGetGroupListReqOp are `RequestOp`s (`reqlast.rs`, kinds
  14 and 15) made by `RustServerOp::NewCreateAccount` and `NewGroupListReq`; with them the 20-line C++
  `ServerRequestOp`, reqhost.rs's `CppReq` and the `EE_WON_HOST_REQ_*` codes went. CreateAccountOp's keys are Rust
  objects (`ElGamal`, `Blowfish`), made in the class's member order (the ElGamal's generator first, then the
  session key's), so one fixed seed gives the same bytes on both halves. A server key that does not load is the
  new `Checked::ServerError` (`SetLastServerError` then the next server). ProfileData (no game user left: the
  account ops take the profile as members) and WONDBMsg.h moved to `tests/won`.
- **A group map as a Rust list of replies.** The group list op keeps every reply it checked; its one reader
  (`RoutingLogic::QueryServerGroupsDone`) reads them again with the original's own statements
  (`RouteGroupListOf` over `RouteGroupListReqReply`) into a connection-less inner op's map for `SyncGroups`. Cheaper
  than a Rust group record and its accessors, and the record-building stays the one template the connection ops
  use. A reply's non-record events set the inner op's flags, which the next request sends: the Rust op keeps them.
- **Random keys in a golden.** `ee_won_random_test_seed(base)` makes the system seed `base + use count` (for the
  drivers only; the Rust replay builds the generators from `random::test_seed` instead, since parallel tests share
  the counter). The driver sets it again before making each half's op.
- **HTTPGetOp on the base** (`httpget.rs`): every step, 18 host codes (the socket's connected test, kill, status
  and blocking line receive, the file's stat, `time`, the cache entry's reads and writes, the receive op's skip,
  binary and modify time, the web proxy host, a new HTTP get, another RustServerOp's results and setters). The
  redirect's child op is made through the host (`EE_WON_HOST_NEW_HTTP_GET`), set and read through
  `EE_WON_HOST_HOSTOP_SET` / `_NUM` / `_BYTES`: the original half does the same, so the traces agree and the child's
  own steps are the same sequences again. The web proxy file stays C++ (read once per process when the first op is
  made; the constructors' growing file name prefix, unobservable, is gone).
- **GetHTTPDocumentOp on the base** (`httpdoc.rs`): its downloads are child HTTP gets, its MOTD flag read one
  `fgetc` host call; the C++ side keeps the construction (the cache file names from the WON directory, the ignored
  path files), the language's lower case and `GetHttpDocument` (the cache file's read). Its readers (InitLogic,
  MOTDCtrl, TOUDialog, LobbyEvents, EEWonNet) read by number: mechanical.
- **Goldens first.** `golden_reqlast.txt` (`won_reqlast_test`, 1000 sequences); `golden_hostop.txt`'s `H` (300) and
  `D` (180) sequences appended, the earlier part byte for byte; the Rust replays port the stand-in's new answers.
  Driver checks 0 failed; mutations fail them (57,440; 312; 7,305) and the replays. A first recording printed a
  server status of -1 as the invalid header the driver encoded as -1: encode an invalid header as a flag.
- **The UB abort in `reqops::tests::contest_through_the_abi`** was the test's: `values(&[.., b(b"ab")])` built the
  C ABI's values from a temporary array dropped at the end of the statement, so `ee_won_reqops_new` copied freed
  bytes (the debug `copy_nonoverlapping` check stopped it when the allocator had reused the block). 13 of 200 runs
  aborted before the fix, 0 after. Any helper returning raw pointers into its argument needs the argument bound.
- **The original's undefined corners, defined.** A NULL reply line reads as empty; a NULL group list reply as an
  empty one; a document callback's id other than 0 or 1 (an index past the arrays) is taken modulo 2;
  OpFinished's `fclose(NULL)` is not done.
- **Not moved, and why.** AuthContext's remaining C++, the peer auth objects and the certificate classes (item 3 of
  the round): not started this round.

  file spec's delete in the original; a first version showed it after (the golden caught it), so the load is one put
  that carries the message (`EE_SCREENS_TEXT_MG_QUICK_LOAD`). The chat's Enter is one event object for the hot key

- **Golden drivers** (scratch, `build/sc8`: `main_game_driver.cpp`, `chat_driver.cpp`, `hotkeys_driver.cpp`,
  `drv.py`; the old headers under `orig/inc`, which `drv.py` now puts first for an `orig*` unit): each one session of
  2,000 cases drawing an event first (all 38 main game kinds; the chat's 15; the hot keys' groups, aircraft and
  unit selections with the creators' arguments), perturbing a persistent world and printing it, then every call.
  Identical old against new on seeds 1-4 (25,000 cases each for 2-4); the round-4 menus and round-7 options drivers
  relinked over the new host still print their goldens. Mutations checked: the speed's range ends, the hidden
  units' moved flag, the clock's cycle, the behaviour button's first match, the chat radios' cycle, the log's
  empty line, the cheat switch, the next unit's fallback, the closest's strict compare, the contained aircraft's
  full hit points, the idle military's speed: each fails its replay.
- **Lessons:**
  - The drivers' fakes must set what the code reads, not what a fake setter records: `GetDisplayMode` is inline
    (`mDisplayMode`), so a state written only to the fake `SetDisplayMode`'s table made every case take one branch;
    the first golden "agreed" with a wrong host until the state was written to the member.
  - A golden that never reaches a rule cannot pin it: the contained aircraft's full hit points rule passed its
    mutation until the driver drew aircraft families and ammunition (and containers) often enough; the hidden units'
    walk needed units in the world's list. Run a mutation per rule.
  - Units whose fields are the unit store's (`EEUnitStoreField`) call `EEUnitStoreWrote` on every write: a driver
    that writes them needs a no-op for it (an unresolved call to 0 otherwise).
  - `::gWorld` in a unit defeats the drivers' `#define gWorld (*gFakeWorld)`: the chat units' driver copies drop the
    `::` (`build/sc8/orig2`). A global object with an out-of-line constructor (`GEViewport gU4E8F08`) is faked the
    same way (`#define gU4E8F08 (*gFakeViewport)`).
  - Git Bash rewrites `/DNAME` in an environment variable into a path: pass `-DNAME` to clang-cl.
  - A comment change in `tools/eedata/` changes the converter code's hash (`open_data.json`) and would rebuild the
    open tree; leave the converters alone in a screens round.
- **What the harness reaches:** the tour's F3 input check (`fixture_game.py --input-check`: the main game form's F3
  hot key, `EE_SCREENS_MG_PAUSE`); the orders' queued steps and the box selection's add mode hold Shift (the main
  game form's Shift hot key: `EE_SCREENS_MG_ENTER_SHIFT` / `_EXIT_SHIFT`, the shift mode messages); the zoom hot keys,
  the wheel and the arrow keys' scroll are not moved (`EEUIEHotKeyZoom`, `EEUIEWheelZoom`, `EEUIEKeyboardScroll`).
  `tools/harness` names none of the deleted classes but in comments (`ai_game.py`'s now name the codes; selftest ALL
  PASS). **Only a person reaches:** the other hot keys (groups, unit selection, aircraft, follow, perspective, the
  clock, hidden units, the cheats, the speed keys, the behaviour menu, F1's return to the editor, F4's quick save and
  loads, the media dump), the main game form's buttons (statistics, diplomacy, chat, the civilization builder, the
  options button, the chat log button), the chat form and the chat log. Network code: quick save sends
  `EEMLoadOrSaveGame` to every player; only a multiplayer game sends it over the wire.
- **Behaviour:** none intended where the original was defined. The main game form's pause posts and drops its
  `EEAUserPauseGame` reference as before; the options menu's pause still keeps it (the shared host op takes the flag).

## R5a.8: the AI host's leaves in Rust: the next engine's save blocks, the AI manifest and seat choice, the name tables (ee_ai; branch rust-ai1, 2026-11-12)

The first round of the AI lane (RUST_PLAN R5a.8). The owner's rules for it: the AI work happens on main, almost all
in Lua; the Lua AI is not at parity with the C++ classic AI, so the classic stays; this lane moves only what cannot
change how an AI plays and stays merge-friendly with main's ongoing Lua/C++ AI work. `EECPNextUnits`, `Tactics`,
`Army` and `View` are main's (36 commits on `EECPNextUnits.cpp` in November): of them only `EECPNextUnits.cpp`'s save
block's two functions changed here, nothing else.

- **What moved** (`rust/crates/ee_ai`, 25 tests):
  - `next_save.rs`: the "EENS" block (`EECPNextLua.cpp` `EECPNextEncodeState`/`DecodeState`): the fields' order,
    versions 1-4, the reader's limits (256 events, `kNextMaxOrders` results, 1,000 groups, 2,048 spots per list, read
    and dropped past them; a group id past the results read and dropped). The C++ fills an `EeAiNextSave` view of its
    state (its own lists' pointers, valid during the call) and copies a decoded block's view back;
  - `units_save.rs`: the "EENU" block (`EECPNextUnits.cpp` `EECPUnitsSaveState`/`LoadState`): the lists go over in
    the C++ containers' order and come back into them (a set's insert, a map's assignment: a repeated key behaves as
    before). The limits `EECPNextUnits.cpp` owns (`kMaxEvents`, `kMaxRemembered`, `kMaxTrades`, the event kinds) come
    with each decode, so a change there needs no Rust change; the format's own (2^20 held and forwards, 256 hurt
    spots, 64 marks) are Rust's;
  - `json.rs`, `manifest.rs`: `EECPEngine.cpp`'s JSON reader (the same documents accepted, the same first error and
    line; numbers as C `strtod` reads a whole decimal one), the entries' checks in their order and every log line;
    `EECPAIToGameText` on `ee_plat_core::utf8`. The C++ still reads the file, answers whether a script exists (a
    callback inside `ee_ai_manifest_read`), writes the lines and the summary (the folder hash is C++);
  - `seat.rs`: `EECPChoiceByName` and `EECPEngineResolve` (the 32-bit hash pool). EE_AI_ENGINE's list is still split
    in C++ (`EECPEngineOverrides`, calling the choice by name);
  - `names.rs`: `EECPNextCodeName`, `EECPNextReasonName`, the two event-kind tables ("?" in the trace, "unknown" in the
    script's view) and the class and tech names by data id (`EECPNextClassName`/`TechName`/`ClassByName`/`TechByName`'s
    tables; the C++ still builds them from `EEDbRowIds` once). `kNextResourceNames` stays a C++ table.
  - C++ deleted: the two block codecs (`EECPNextPut`, the getters, the army encode/decode), the JSON reader, the id,
    module and text checks, the name switches and the names map (the four files: 880 lines out, 385 in, most of them the views' marshalling).
- **The golden driver** (scratch, `build/ai1_golden`): `make_driver.py` cuts the functions out of a source tree (git
  `78035043` or the work tree) by their markers and compiles them into one exe with fakes (the manifest's file, the
  script files: every path without "missing", the log, `EEDbRowIds`, the unit class table) linked with `ee_rust.lib`.
  Its cases: 60 generated next states and 80 per-unit states (every tenth past the decoder's limits), each encoded
  (length, FNV-1a 64, the first three in hex) and 16 changed blocks of each (versions 1-3 by dropping the newer parts,
  bad versions, cuts, a byte more, a bad magic, four flipped bytes) decoded onto another generated state and encoded
  again; 427 manifest documents (the real `ai/ais.json`, CRLF and BOM copies, 60 hand-made entries alone and between
  two good ones, 30 broken documents, 260 random edits of a small manifest); the choices by name, seven EE_AI_ENGINE
  lists and a hash of 15,000 resolves for the first twelve manifests; the name tables. `golden.rs` replays the generator
  step for step and checks every line; the same driver over the new forwarders prints the identical file (5,325 lines),
  and 40 real blocks (the EENS and EENU blocks of boom, classic_lua and ageofai saves at 1000 and 1900 s, cut out of the
  decompressed players chunk) decode and encode to the same bytes in both and in Rust (`real_blocks`, ignored: it needs
  `EE_AI_BLOCKS`).
- **Two C++ evaluation-order traps in the driver itself**: `a(g.Next()) + b(g.Next())` on two `std::string`s is a
  call whose arguments are unsequenced; the generator's draws went into locals first. Python's `write_text` on Windows

  the C++ view both. The rest of `EECPNextUnits.cpp` is as main wrote it.
- The Rust gate's `ee_won` test `reqops::tests::contest_through_the_abi` aborted once under full load
  (`ptr::copy_nonoverlapping` precondition) and passed alone and on the gate's rerun: a race in that crate's tests,
  not this lane's.

  ageofai seeds 2-3 identical again (decisions, checksum lines, saved blocks); the five capture profiles PASS (oracle
  494, late 499, space 501, calamity 526, missile 60 digests); `saveload --settings all --seeds 2-3 --at 1000,1900`
  as before except `next` 2/4: seeds 2 and 3 at 1000 s part 647 and 1217 ticks after the load, and the unmodified

  0.05))`, not the up key's order); the tribute amounts' `(long)` casts are x64's `cvttss2si` (`i32::MIN` out of

    `extern template` for importers) cannot be faked by a specialization; the driver defines it under its decorated
    name with clang's `__asm__` label (`extern "C" long F(const void*, unsigned long&) __asm__("?GetCurrentSelection@...")`).
  - The driver's random state must stay inside what the original survives: a current player whose id is 0 put the
    OK button's rows below 19 and crashed the unmodified unit; the mouse's X and Y entities are never checked for
    NULL there (only the middle button and the wheel are).

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 13 (AuthContext's login data, GetVersionOp and FindPatchOp as Rust objects)

Branch `rust-won-net13`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 12. Nothing in the game reaches this code but
an Internet login (AuthContext's login data: the lobby's login, account and certificate requests) or nothing at all
(GetVersionOp and FindPatchOp had no caller); the servers are gone. Only the drivers and the Rust replays exercise
it; the shims' new lines only compile.

- **AuthContext's login data as one Rust object** (`authlogin.rs`): the user name and password, the secret file and
  its secrets, the communities (CD key, valid flag, file hashes), the CD-key joins, the user data, the nicknames,
  each setter of the original and the login request's three blocks, behind its own lock. AuthContext keeps its
  lock, peer data, server context and certificate flow and is otherwise a shim (`mLogin`); its maps, strings,
  secret list and the `AuthLoginCommunityData` type are gone. `GetName`, `GetUserName` and `GetPassword` return
  copies now (EEWonNet and UpdateAccountCtrl read them).
- **The file hashes over the original's stdio loop.** `SetHashFileList` is the MD5 loop over `PlatFOpen` / `fread` /
  `feof` (a `Stream` trait: the C file in the game, the bytes in the replay, the end flag set by a short read as
  the CRT's): sections run across files, the short last one at the end of the last file; a file that does not
  open returns false with the hashes cleared and what was hashed so far kept, as the original.
- **The maps' order is `std::map<std::wstring>`'s on Windows** (UTF-16 units). A POSIX build's 32-bit `wchar_t`
  ordered names above U+FFFF differently; nothing uses such names.
- **GetVersionOp and FindPatchOp are directory request ops** (`verop.rs`, kinds 16 and 17): each ran one GetDirOp
  child and read its entities when it finished, so the Rust op is the directory op itself (made at `RunHook`, its
  flags and path as the original's) reading the listing when it succeeds. Results and queries by number (the
  versions, their descriptions, `CheckVersion`, the patches and the three patch lists through a setter and
  `num_at`). The `SetVersionCompare` hook (no caller) is gone: the compare is `std::string::compare`. Their units,
  headers and the C++ helpers only they used (`FindPatchMsg`, `PatchFilterSet`, `PatchIsFiltered`) moved to
  `tests/won/won_version_msg.h`. New C ABI for bare request ops: `ee_won_reqop_set`, `_num_at`, `_entities`.
- **GetHTTPDocumentOp's C++ helpers moved in** (`httpdoc.rs`): the cache file names (from the WON directory the
  shim passes), the once-per-process path file (closed now; the original left it open), the lower case of the
  product and language, and `GetDocument`'s read through `PlatFOpen`. The web proxy file stays C++: its read is a
  host call in `golden_hostop.txt`'s H traces.
- **Goldens first.** `golden_authlogin.txt` (won_auth_test's login sequences, 300) and `golden_verop.txt`
  (won_verop_test, 600). Drivers 117,983 and 100,000 checks, 0 failed; mutations fail 18,563 and 293 checks and
  the replays.
- **A version's data was read as a C string** (`std::string(mData->data())`): to its first NUL, and past the end
  of a buffer without one. An empty buffer's `data()` is NULL here (ee_won's bytes), which crashed the driver's
  original half: the data is read to its first NUL or its end, both halves.
- **A first golden missed the filter**: the generator's version data used "pt:opt", but the filter line's key is
  "pt" before a space. Check that a golden reaches each branch (count the outcomes) before recording it.
- **Goldens printed on Windows are CR LF** (stdout's text mode); `str::lines` reads both. The new ones are LF.
- **Not moved, and why.** The peer auth objects (PeerAuthOp, PeerAuthServerOp, PeerAuthClient, PeerAuthServer) and
  the certificate classes: not started this round. AuthContext's lock, peer data, server context and the
  certificate flow's hook table stay C++ until the peer auth ops and GetCertOp's objects are Rust.

## R5b.4, fourteenth round: the other classes' ActionChanged as Rust decisions, the stats table, units of no id by object (ee_units actions.rs, stats.rs, store.rs, header_consts.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core14, 2026-11-12)

  the golden recording replaced every USST row anyway.

  `EEUCBuildingPriest::PriestVirtual74` was the basic priest's body (plus a cast with no effect): the temple's
  default is the Rust `basic_priest` decision, the host's conversion-effects operation picks the temple's own
  `HideConversionEffects` (the temple is no `EEUCBasicPriest`).
- **What stays C++, and where.** A branch that is more than one call (the landable's takeoff, landing approach,
  secondary target and path; the helicopters' paths to the goal; the airplane's space-map circling side and holding
  pattern; the planet spaceship's holding pattern; the air animal's path and dying spin) is one host operation whose
  body is the original's statements, kept in the class's own file (`EE<Class>...` functions declared in
  ee/EEUnitUpdate.h) next to the file's local declarations and constants, not moved into the host. Rust decides
  which run and in which order; the random draws of circling (the air animal's, the planet spaceship's) are reads at
  their place.
- **Every copied constant checked by script, now a test.** header_consts.rs reads every `const` of ee_units' sources
  whose name copies the original's (ACTION_, GOAL_, CATEGORY_, MOVEMENT_, UNIT_TYPE_, FAMILY_, RESOURCE_, TRIGGER_ and
  the EE_ forms), maps it to the header's name, evaluates both and fails on a difference or a name the headers lack.
  This round's 49 new action constants were generated from EEUnitAction.h by script and pass it.
- **The stats as a table keyed by object, versioned.** A unit's `mStats` is its player's `EEUnitClassUpgrade` of its
  class, changed in place by upgrades: no holder fits. The table (stats.rs) has one record per stats object; the C++
  reports an object at every function that writes one (found by a script over every `EEUnitClassUpgrade*`/`mStats`
  base: `Init`, `SetMaxVelocity`, `SetRange`, `SetDeathSound`, `LoadMedia`, the improvements' `ChangeLevel`, the
  civilization builder's `EECBApplyStat`/`EECBUpgradeArmor`, the scenario events' `ApplyEventAttribute`/
  `ApplyEventGatherRate`, `EEModifyUnitAttribute`, `EEUpgradeHitPoints`) through a scope object that reports on every
  return, and drops it in the destructor. The version counts the reports that changed the record. The unit record's
  `stats` names the object (field 48). USCK fills every unit's stats object and compares it with the table (a stale
  record is a mismatch: a writer the script missed shows there, in the profiles that run it). The death sound is in
  the record but stays a host read: the media loader sets it.
- **Units of no id: a scenario's path points, the shots.** The triggers lane's scenario profile found the store wrong
  in every played scenario: a scenario's path points (type 0xdf, complex, on the map's chain) are in their players'
  lists, every one of id 0xffffffff, and records by id collapsed them into one. The out-of-sync checksum's flags 1 and
  2 (from the store since the eighth and ninth rounds) and combat's store reads were wrong there; random maps have no
  such unit, so no gate saw it. The store now keeps every unit of id 0xffffffff in a second table by object (`insert`

## R5b.4, fifteenth round: the goal queues as goal ids (ee_units goals.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core15, 2026-11-13)

- **The ids were already there.** Every goal has `mID` (`++sGoalCounter` at construction; the load path draws one
  back and reads the saved id): the saves' goal ids. So "goal queues as ids" is a mirror, not a new numbering: each
  queue container (`EEUnitVectorItem`, one of a complex unit's `mGoalQueues`) is its goals' ids in Rust, by the
  container's address with its unit, and the unit record carries the active goal's id (field 49) beside its kind.
  Ids are not unique across clones (a cloned goal keeps its id), so the mirror is per container, never a map by id.
- **A unit's queue index is its container's address order.** `mGoalQueues` is one vector, so a unit's containers
  sorted by address are its queues in index order; a reallocation copies them to new addresses (the copies report,
  the old ones' destructors drop their mirrors), and no read runs inside it.
- **The deque as a holder, as the store's fields.** `EEGoalDeque` wraps the container's `std::deque<EEUnitGoal*>`: it
  reads as the deque (size, elements, front/back, const iterators, `Get()` for a copy) and every change reports the
  whole list (queues are a few goals). Giving out no writable reference or iterator made the compiler list every
  writer and every reader that had bound a `std::deque&`: 18 errors over 11 files, all readers but the container's
  copy constructor and `operator=` (their element writes became `Set`). `DeleteVectorContents` needs a type named
  `iterator`: the holder's is the const one (the loop only reads).
- **Bash heredocs on this machine eat backslash escapes.** A Python edit sent through a quoted heredoc wrote a real
  newline where the C++ string had `\n` (the compiler's "expected expression" found it). Write edit scripts with the
  file tool and run them, or use the editor tool for strings with escapes.

## R4.4, seventh round: the effects' records, their base classes' Load and Save, the effects' random generator, the smoke generators and smoke puffs whole in Rust (ee_gfx effect_state.rs, ffi_effect.rs; branch rust-gfx13, 2026-11-12)

Effects are simulation state, so the round's golden is a capture record of the C++ first. Graphics Thread C++
(`src/Empire Earth/Graphics Thread/*.cpp`): 25,692 lines before the round; 25,752 with the EFST capture (45 lines,
TEST ONLY) and the emitter's zeroed times; 25,403 after the move (5 units fewer).

- **EFST, the effects' state after every Update** (`EEEffectManager.cpp` `EECaptureEffectStates`): the effects' random
  seed, then per effect of the index in handle order its handle, kind, player, local-only and saved flags and a saved
  effect's own `Save` bytes written into an `FSMemoryFile`: every base class's and leaf's saved state at every tick,
  folded to a count, a length and an FNV-1a 64. Golden lines in all five profiles.
- **Garbage in the saved bytes.** The first golden did not repeat: two runs of one build gave two EFST digests. The
  original's constructors leave members to `SetUp`, to the first step or to a tag point that may not exist
  (`EEE3DParticleEmitter`'s times and the tag point follower's `GETransformation(false)`, `EEE2DImpact`'s tag index
  and start, `EEE2DLightGlow`'s, ...), and a save wrote whatever the heap held; the move changed the heap's reuse and
  with it the garbage, not the game (every other digest equal). Found with a temporary per-effect dump (tick, handle,
  kind, a hash of its bytes; two runs, `diff`, then the bytes of the first differing tick). Fixed at the source for
  every effect: `EEEffect` has class `operator new`/`new[]` that zero the storage (the pools' `new T[]` too), and the
  emitter's constructors zero its times (its tag point follower starts at the identity). The golden lines were
  recorded again from the C++ effects with only those fixes, built in a temporary worktree (`git worktree add
  build/gx13/before`, its own staging root `C:/EEX-gfx9-drv`), and runs now repeat bit for bit. A capture record over
  saved bytes finds such members: run it twice on one build before trusting its golden.
- **The records (`effect_state.rs` `EeGfxEffectRecord`).** One `#[repr(C)]` record per effect: `EEEffect`'s kind,
  handle, player, region and three flags, `EEEffect3D`'s transformation, `EEEffect2D`'s position, one bounding radius
  for both (an effect is one or the other) and the moved leaves' state (`smoke`, `plume`). The effect's constructor
  makes it (`EEEffect::mRecord`, a default member initializer, so every constructor, the inline load-time ones too,
  makes one; `ee_gfx_effect_record_new`) and `~EEEffect` frees it; the C++ members are references into it (`int32_t&
  mKind = mRecord->kind`, `GETransformation& mTransformation = *reinterpret_cast<...>(&mRecord->transformation)`), so
  the 60 effect classes' readers and writers kept their spelling. The effect store indexes the effects; the records
  are reached through them. Effects are not copyable (they never were copied). `EEEffectHandle::mValue` is a
  `uint32_t` (the record's; `unsigned long` was 8 bytes on LP64).
- **Load and Save** of `EEEffect`, `EEEffect3D`, `EEEffect2D` and the moved leaves are Rust over a typed file
  (`EeGfxEffectFile`: `is_open`, `read`/`write` of `u32`, `i32`, `f32`, `bool`, each the `FSFile` call of that type,
  so a debug file's text is unchanged too): the same reads and writes in the same order, the same first error, the
  base results the original ignores ignored, the 2D parts through callbacks (the C++ keeps the vector, the graphic
  objects and their media loads). `EEEffect::Load` resolves the graphic effect after the reads (its media load reads
  no file). Each FFI call works on a copy of the record and writes it back: no Rust reference to it lives across a
  callback.
- **The region** (`MoveToPoint`/`MoveToTransformation`, one `MoveToRegion`): the region under a point in Rust, the
  map's region lists in C++.
- **The effects' random generator** (the original's file-static `URandom` of `EEEffect.cpp`): a Rust `Mutex<URandom>`
  (seed 1, never reseeded, not saved); `GetRandom`, `GetEffectRandomFloat`, `GetEffectRandomLong` forward. A Rust step
  takes the lock per draw, never across a callback: the effects a step creates draw too, in between.
- **The smoke generators whole** (`EEE3DSmokeGenerator`, which is now also the original's `EEE3DDamageSmoke`, kind
  0x2c, and `EEE3DDestructionSmoke`, kind 0x1e; both classes deleted): the tick (the timers, the end tests, the
  spread draws, the damage smoke's health interval with the original's unsigned `mTime2 - mTime1`, the destruction
  smoke's empty puff that still draws and counts down), the destruction smoke's set-up lines (`ee_ge`'s yaw-pitch-roll
  turn), load and save by kind; the C++ reads the unit, its tag points and the graphic effect into a plain tick record

- **The smoke puffs whole** (`EEE2DSmokePlume`, now also the original's `EEE2DVelocityParticle`, kind 0xc, deleted):
  the constructor's rotation and brightness draws (the `max`/`min` macros' comparisons), both ticks (the puff's by the
  tick's seconds, the velocity particle's by its tick time, damped by int param 1), load and save; the C++ keeps the

No tour run.

## R5a.8, second round: the Lua runtime in Rust over the same Lua (ee_ai lua_value, lua_host; branch rust-ai2, 2026-11-12)

Steps 1 and 2 of the plan in RUST_PLAN R5a.8. `EECPLua.cpp` went from 1,484 lines to 429 (the value tree's C++
methods, the ops table Rust reads and builds the tree through, the forwarders, `EECPLuaReadFromFolder`); `EECPLua.h`
224 -> 209 (the state's private members are a handle, its counters out-of-line calls).

- **What moved** (`rust/crates/ee_ai`):
  - `lua_value.rs`: the key order and equality, the tree's equality and text, the "EELM" value encoding and its
    decoder (the offset and the error where it stops, the value untouched on a failure), the seed, SplitMix64. The
    algorithms read any tree through a `Tree` trait: a C++ `EECPLuaValue` through `kEECPLuaTreeOps` (one call per
    value: its scalars and its vectors' storage with the element sizes) or a Rust `Value`. A decode or a conversion
    builds a Rust `Value` first and copies it into the C++ tree (set, push, field);
  - `lua_host.rs`: `EECPLuaState`'s body: the state (the allocator's user data is the Rust host; `From` answers the
    C++ owner), the libraries and the sandbox, print/tostring/string.format/setmetatable/require/each/ai.keys/
    ai.random, the count hook and `Charge`, `Run`/`Init`/`Step`/`CallOptional`/`LoadPersonality`/`Reload`, the
    converter both ways (and `CheckMemory`'s walk), `SaveMemory`/`RestoreMemory` (encoded from the Rust value, no C++
    tree between). `require`'s reader is the ops' `read` on the owner: the text stays in the C++ state's buffer until
    it has compiled (`luaL_loadbufferx` does not raise), then is released, as the C++ local was;
  - `lua_api.rs`: the API the host calls, declared `extern "C"` over `mlua-sys`'s types and constants (below);
  - `lua_ffi.rs`: the C ABI. `EECPLuaStatusName` is Rust's too.
- **Every Lua API call is the C++'s, in its order**, so the state allocates the same blocks: the golden driver
  (`build/ai2_golden`, the unmodified `EECPLua.cpp` of 419b4b81 with `ee_lua.c` and `ee_rust.lib`) prints memory used
  and peak after each of 141 chunks and commands (sandbox names, 17 formats and the refused ones, metatables, each over
  2,000 keys, the random ranges, require's bad names, error objects, results that cannot convert, budgets, charges,
  memory caps down to a state that cannot open, the personality's entries, saves, restores of cut and flipped blocks,
  reload, check memory): identical over the Rust state. The `PushSortedKeys` userdata keeps the C++ entry's size (40
  bytes), `print` keeps its `luaL_Buffer`, `string.format`'s scan keeps `strchr`'s NUL (a NUL in a format counts as a
  flag and as a float conversion).
- **longjmp through Rust on Windows** (the finding of this round): `mlua-sys` declares Lua's functions `extern
  "C-unwind"`. The MSVC CRT's `longjmp` is an SEH unwind, and with the release profile's `panic = "abort"` rustc puts
  an abort pad around every call of a function that may unwind: luatest aborted at its first script error with
  "panic in a function that cannot unwind". The tests (`panic = "unwind"`) passed, so only the release library shows
  it. Declared `extern "C"` (`lua_api.rs`), the calls get no pad in either profile; the functions Lua calls stay
  `extern "C-unwind"` (no pad under `panic = "unwind"` either), and nothing between a protected call and a raise owns a
  destructor. Step 3 (mlua's high-level API) meets the same: mlua raises through its own `C-unwind` frames, so it
  needs `panic = "unwind"` for the library or the same non-unwinding declarations; check a script error under the
  release build first.
- **Tests with the real Lua**: `build.rs` compiles `src/ThirdParty/lua/ee_lua.c` (cc) for the crate's own tests only
  (not for a release or cross build); `lua_host.rs` links it under `cfg(test)`, and ee_rust's test binary leaves ee_ai
  out. The test replays the driver's part B on the Rust host, memory counts included: Lua compiled by cl allocates as
  the game's clang-cl build does. A chunk with a NUL byte: `Run` takes a C string, so the test passes `strlen`'s length.
- **cbindgen**: `Option<alias of an extern fn>` in a public Rust struct and the imported Lua declarations both came out
  as `template<typename T = void> struct Option;` and stopped the header splitter: the module of imports carries
  `/// cbindgen:ignore` (the bare annotation: with more text on the line it is not recognised) and the config's
  function pointers are spelt inline. The splitter now reads `extern "C-unwind"` definitions (`ee_ai_lua_charge`);
  cbindgen cannot spell a `C-unwind` function pointer, so `EeAiLuaConfig::open` is a `void*`.
- **Line endings**: Python's `write_text` on Windows wrote CR LF into LF files (a whole-file diff); every edit since
  goes through bytes.
- **Gates of both steps**: luatest 136/136; the driver identical; boom, classic_lua and ageofai seeds 2-3 (2700 s,
  saves at 1000/1900 s, `EE_AI_SAVE_CHECK=1`) identical to the unmodified exe (decisions, checksum lines, the saved
  EENS/EENU blocks, every savecheck same, no next.error); oracle seeds 2-3 identical to `ref`; `saveload --settings
  next` as `tools/saveload_expect.txt` (647, 1217, END, END); the Rust gate PASS. Only the EE-SIM and the tests ran:
  the Lua AI's lobby/tour path has no new code here (the state is the same object behind the same handle).

## R5a.8, third round: the per-unit bindings' Lua helpers on the raw API (ee_ai units_lua; branch rust-ai3, 2026-11-12)

The lead's decisions for step 3: keep `panic = "abort"` and the hand-written `extern "C"` declarations of
`lua_api.rs`; no mlua high-level API; the bindings on the raw API, so that a Lua error never crosses a Rust frame
that cannot unwind; the first check on the release library: a script error under luatest must not abort.

- **What moved**: `units_lua.rs`, the helpers every `ai.*` binding of `EECPNextUnits.cpp` calls: `ReadIds`,
  `OptInt`/`OptBool`/`OptString`/`OptNear`/`OptAmount`, `ClassArg` (the class lookup by name stays C++, passed as a
  function pointer), `LayerArg` (an index; the C++ maps it to its vector), `ReadFilter` (the filter copied into a
  `repr(C)` mirror and back), `Result` (with the reason names), `SetInt`/`SetStr`/`SetBool`, `PushSorted` (sorts the
  C++'s `std::pair<long long, long>` vector in place through a same-layout Rust struct); and the binding `ai.used`
  (`lua_host.rs`). The 79 bindings stay C++ over the game's objects: their bodies are unchanged, the helpers' bodies
  are one-line forwarders (`EECPNextUnits.cpp` 4,390 -> 4,304 lines), so main's work on the bindings merges as before.
- **A Lua error through a Rust helper**: a script's `__index` runs inside `lua_getfield`. The helpers are
  `extern "C-unwind"` over `extern "C"` declarations and own nothing with a destructor; the error is the script's.
  luatest has four new checks (`ai.optx` through `ee_ai_units_opt_int`: an error raised by `__index`, the same under
  pcall, a budget raised by the hook inside the helper): 141/141 with the release library.
- **`long` stays `long`**: the C++ cast `lua_tointeger` to `long` (32 bits on Windows) before comparing (`ClassArg`'s
  `>= 0`, `OptAmount`'s clamp); the Rust uses `c_long` at the same points.
- **The golden driver** (`build/ai3_golden`): the helpers cut out of `EECPNextUnits.cpp` (git c265af97), a real Lua
  with a counting allocator, 47 Lua values (integers past 32 bits, floats, arrays past 4,000 ids, holes, `near`,
  type lists past 16, metatables whose `__index` answers, raises or hands back tables), each helper in its own pcall,
  then the result, field and sorted-list pushers: 529 lines with the stack top and the byte count after each,
  identical over the forwarders; `units_lua.rs`'s test replays it. One trap of the driver's own: `printf`'s arguments
  run right to left under clang-cl, so three `OptBool` calls in one `printf` asked `idle` before `flag` (seen only in
  which `__index` error came first); the Rust replay calls them in that order.
- **Bare constants in headers**: `pub const MAX_IDS` landed in `ee_ai.h` and clashed with ee_netmsg's (`ee_netmsg.h`
  gained `#include "ee_ai.h"`); round 2's `HOOK_STEP` and `MAX_DEPTH` were there too. All are crate-private now, and a
  `repr(C)` array's length is a literal. The helpers take the state as `void*`: `ee_ai.h` is included by files that
  do not include `lua.h`.
- **Gates** (on db8752c8): build `--sim` 0/0; luatest 141/141; boom, classic_lua and ageofai seeds 2-3 identical to the
  unmodified exe (decisions, checksum lines, saved blocks, savecheck same); oracle seeds 2-7 identical to `ref`;
  `saveload --settings next` as the expect file (647, 1217, END, END); the Rust gate PASS; captures at seeds 2-3:
  oracle, late, space, calamity and missile PASS. Only EE-SIM and the tests ran: no tour.

## R6 WON round 22: InputBox, Label and Splitter whole in Rust over the component op table (ee_won inputobj.rs, labelobj.rs, splitobj.rs; branch rust-r6-won22, 2026-11-12)

Measured as rounds 18-21 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi`, `wc -l`): 90,554 at
the branch's start (round 21 and the other lanes merged into rust) -> 89,985 after InputBox (-569) -> 89,916 after
Label (-69) -> 89,535 after Splitter (-381): -1,019 in all.

- **The pattern, unchanged from round 21.** Each leaf keeps its C++ class (the type the lobby, the configs and the
  subclasses hold; its vtable) with one-line inline forwarders to `ee_won_<leaf>_call`, and the Rust object makes
  every call out through its own host function in `WONGUI/GuiHost.cpp` (`ee_won_guicpp_input_call`, `_label_call`,
  `_split_call`), all over the one op enum `guihost.rs` `EeWonGuiOp`. The component services (`ComponentOp`) are
  shared; this round added the base focus and paint calls, `SetSize` (which calls the component's `Virtual08` back
  when the size changes: the goldens' hosts do the same), the default cursor (three more standard cursors),
  `FireEvent` (`EeWonGuiEvent`), the clipboard, the input box's font measures and text copies, the label's wrapped
  text and background, and a container's children, buttons and events.
- **InputBox** (`inputobj.rs`): the shown and real (password) text, selection and drag, scroll, blink, padding and
  text rectangle, history, limits and paint. `GetText()` returns a reference, so the C++ keeps two `GUIString`
  copies (`mText` the shown one the font measures, `mRealText`), stored by the op `TextStore` at the end of each
  text change (before the change event). The filter stays a C++ function pointer (`LanPortDialog` sets
  `NumericFilter`, which now reads `GetSelStart()`); the op `Filter` answers 2 without one. The fields the configs
  and `SkinnedContainers` wrote (`mMaxChars`, `mSelectOnFocus`, `mMaxInputHistory`, `mLeftPad`) are setters; the
  colours, backgrounds, selection colours and font stay C++ fields. Inward texts are `wchar_t` units (2 bytes on
  Windows; `inputobj::units_in`), outward ones u32 units; a typed or password character is stored as the platform's
  `wchar_t` would (`wunit`). One departure, on both sides of the golden: a history limit of 0 stopped the trim at an
  empty history (the original popped an empty deque).
- **Label** (`labelobj.rs`): colour, alignments, padding, fit-to-text height, desired size and paint. The wrapped text
  stays C++ (the test fixture reads its text for `ui-state.txt`); `SetText` sets it in the inline forwarder, then
  the Rust steps run (`TextSet`). Small: most of the label is the wrapped text, which 46 outside references use.
- **Splitter** (`splitobj.rs`): panes, bars and drag handles, maximise buttons, split, percentages (doubles), minimum
  panes, drag and maximised quadrant. Children are borrowed `Component*`s; the drag handles and buttons are held
  with `ChildHold` / `ChildRelease` (the original's `SmartPtr`s, given back in the original's member order). The two
  components it makes are ops (`NewDragComponent` drops the creator's reference inside the op, as the original's
  `SmartPtr` left its block; `NewSizedComponent` returns it held and Rust releases it after `AddSplitter`). A header
  slip worth remembering: replacing a class by searching for the first `};` after `class X {` stops at an inner
  enum's `};` (it did here: the compile caught it).
- **The goldens** (`tests/won/won_inputobj_test.cpp`, `won_labelobj_test.cpp`, `won_splitobj_test.cpp`): each holds the
  original's methods with every C++ call replaced by the op that makes it, and runs them and the Rust object over one
  scripted host: 20,000 sequences each; InputBox 3,859,829 trace lines (events whose handler sets the text, clears
  it into the history or selects all; the numeric filter reading the box back; a filter that changes the text; the
  clipboard), Label 1,960,872, Splitter 5,335,120 (every reference given back); all identical. Mutations (Delete as
  Backspace; the label's minimum wrap width; a bar's drag axis) fail 11,435 / 3,661 / 3,050 sequences. The
  `golden_*obj.txt` files (40 to 44 sequences of 16 calls) are replayed op for op by `cargo test`. A `%llx` of a
  negative argument is 16 hex digits: the replay parses it as u64 first.

  each commit). Only the lobby reaches these classes, so only the lead's LAN game and lobby captures check them:
  - InputBox: the LAN lobby's name box, the chat line on the LAN lobby and in the game room (typing, Enter: the
    return event clears it into the history, as the golden's handler does), the port box of the LAN port dialog

    boxes' text, caret and selection and the disabled look.
  - Label: every caption and status line of the lobby and the dialogs (the captures' text placement and colour).
  - Splitter: the game room (`GameStagingCtrl.cfg` `TopChat`: the chat left, the player list right, minimum 300 /

## R6: the game screens, eleventh round: the loading screen, the chat log and the line graph's axis texts in Rust (ee_screens splash.rs, chat_log.rs, post_game.rs; branch rust-screens11, 2026-11-12)

  The line graph's axis texts moved without deleting a unit (`EEUIPGSLineGraph.cpp` stays the toolkit's control

  (`UWideString::Load`/`Save` with its Windows-1252 conversion, `GEColor::Load`/`Save`). The original attached its

  is clang's 64-bit `cvttss2si` kept to 32 bits, so 2^32 and above wrap and NaN or values past 2^63 become 0, which
  `GetMinutesAndSeconds` replaces with the game's time. The golden's edges (2^32, NaN, infinities) pin both.

  Rust (each with a mutation that fails it), relinked over the new host printing the same on seeds 1-4.

    driver's calloc'ed control needs none.

## R5b.4, sixteenth round: the goal queues' record and update, the patrol goal whole in Rust (ee_units goals.rs, patrol.rs; EEUGRust; branch rust-r5b4-core16, 2026-11-13)

- **The record from the mirror.** The queue mirror now holds the goals' objects and kinds beside their ids, and the
  timer (reported by `AddTime`, `ResetTimer`, the copies and the load's reads). `EEGoalQueueContainer::Save` writes
  from it and `Load` is a Rust sequence; the host makes the typed `FSFile` calls (the debug file formats each type, so
  a byte is `Write(unsigned char)`, never raw bytes) and the goals' own `Save`/`CreateGoal`+`Load`. Saves are
  byte-for-byte the same format; saveload's oracle setting stays END on every save.
- **The queues' update.** The classes' goal-queue step (started, non-empty queues expire at start + time, then
  `RefreshGoals`/`RefreshActiveGoal`) reads the mirror per queue: the refresh may change the next one. One host op
  keeps the one USST note.
- **A whole goal class to Rust, and what it costs.** `EEUGPatrol` is gone: a patrol goal is an `EEUGRust` (one C++
  class for goals whose state and bodies are Rust's: the base goal's fields and vtable stay, every virtual is one
  call), its state a Rust table by goal object. The callers moved to `EEUGRust::NewPatrol`, `EEPatrolGoalCast` and
  accessors. The first class costs as much as it saves (C++ +413 -414): the generic class and its host table are as
  long as the class. The next goals reuse both, so each further class deletes its whole file.
- **A broad regex over a file edits more than the class.** `theGoal->mTarget` -> the patrol accessor also caught the
  attack goal's `theGoal->mTarget` in an earlier case of `EEActiveGroup::Plan`; the compiler named it. Anchor such
  replacements to the declaration they follow.
- **Coverage by a temporary print.** The oracle and late games never patrol; the scenario profile's games create
  routed patrols and step them, so its captures gate the move. No saveload game holds a patrol goal: its record is
  unit tests only.

## R6 WON round 23: ListArea whole in Rust, its readers on accessors (ee_won listobj.rs; branch rust-r6-won23, 2026-11-12)

Measured as rounds 18-22 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi`, `wc -l`): 88,296 at
the branch's start (round 22 merged with rust) -> 87,629 after the ListArea commit (-667, the two accessor commits
included).

- **Accessors first, in their own commits.** The lobby read ListArea's members in 12 units: `mSelItem` (combo
  boxes, menus, the friend, user, game user, room, server, adapter and file lists, the game options) became
  `GetSelItem()`, `mPaintWidth` (the items' paints) a new `GetPaintWidth()`, the game user list's `mItems.size()`
  `GetNumItems()`. Then the family's own writes: `MultiListArea::SetSortColumn` sets the sort type through
  `SetSortTypeOnly` (no sort, as the original's field write), its paint the paint width through `SetPaintWidth`,
  `MultiListHeader` reads `GetSortType`, and MultiListItem's and TreeItem's MouseExit clear the list's mouse item
  through `ClearMouseItem` (the field only, not the virtual `NotifyMouseItemGone`, as before).
- **The move** (`listobj.rs`): the items (a reference held on each, as the original's `SmartPtr` vector), the top
  line, the list flags, the batch depth, the paint width, the sort type, the current, keyboard and mouse items and
  the selection walk; every method of ListArea.cpp and SetSortType. The C++ `ListArea` keeps the font, the colours,
  the selection colours, the sort function and the item tool tip; its virtuals are forwarders, and the Rust calls
  the list's own virtuals back through the C++ object (`VirtAdjustPosition`, `VirtSort`,
  `VirtNotifyMouseItemGone`, `VirtListSelChangedHook`), so MultiListArea's, TreeArea's and PopupMenu's overrides run
  and call the base back into Rust. The items stay C++ data (the lobby's item classes), read and set through ops.
- **The sort stays C++'s `std::sort`.** It is not stable: a Rust sort would order equal items differently. The op
  `SortItems` sorts the Rust object's item array (raw pointers) with the original `LineSortPred`, `LowerBound` is
  `std::lower_bound` for the sorted insert, `Less` the predicate RefreshItem tests its neighbours with. The
  original sorted `SmartPtr`s; the same algorithm over raw pointers makes the same comparisons and the same order.
- **RefreshItem's move** permutes the item vector by `SmartPtr` assignments; their AddRef / Release pairs never take
  an item to zero, so the Rust permutes plain pointers and keeps the one reference per item.
- **A dropped statement:** MultiListArea's constructor reserved 11,000 entries of the vector (capacity only).
- **The golden** (`tests/won/won_listobj_test.cpp`): the original's methods with every C++ call replaced by its op,
  against the Rust object over one scripted host (the scroll area's fields and clamp, items with sizes, keys and
  selectable flags, the base size change and the list's virtuals calling the side's ListArea back): 20,000
  sequences of 40 calls (sorted and placed inserts, batches, refreshes that move an item, deletes, ranges, clears,
  every flag, every selection path, the walk, sorting, scrolls, paints, the mouse with every flag, keys),
  12,464,203 trace lines identical, every reference given back. A mutation (the toggle flag's test) fails 6,552
  sequences. `golden_listobj.txt` (45 sequences) is replayed by cargo.
- **Shell lesson:** a Bash tool command whose heredoc holds an odd number of single quotes (a Python `r'''`
  string) fails before running ("unexpected EOF while looking for matching"): the tool wraps the command in single
  quotes. Write such scripts to a file and run the file.
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby (the oracle is unchanged by construction). Only the lobby reaches
  ListArea: the LAN game list and the user list of the LAN lobby, the game room's player list (MultiListArea), the
  combo boxes' drop-downs (the user name, the options), popup menus (right click on a user), the room tree
  (Internet only). The LAN game (joining by the game list's selection and double click) and the lobby captures
  (the lists' rows, selection colours, scroll) are the check. Item tool tips, keyboard navigation and the sort's
  column clicks run only in the golden unless a person uses them.
- **Left:** MultiListArea, MultiListHeader, MultiListItem, TreeArea and TreeItem (now C++ subclasses and items over
  the Rust base), PopupMenu with MenuBehavior, and the scroll bars (Scrollbar has ~50 member reads in 9 units:
  an accessor commit first).

  background label's text when not found) each fail it; a mutation of the scroll flag passed seed 1's golden, which
  never reaches it.
- **Behaviour:** none intended. Only a person reaches the campaign editor (the editors' sub-menu's Campaign Editor;
  no gate opens form 24).
- **Not moved:** the scenario intro's form manager (`EEUISCIFormManager`, 315): its decisions are three extension
  lists and `HasMedia`'s short-circuit; a Rust move replaces each test with a forwarder of the same size, so it
  deletes nothing (the only saving there is a C++ refactor of the three `Open*`). The civilization builder's helpers
  (`EECivilizationBuilder.cpp` 617, `EECBUIListBox` 835) are thin toolkit calls with C++ callers across the builder's
  units; they wait for the builder's files to move.

## A citizen waiting for a gather spot whose goal is no gather (EE-SIM, 2026-11-12)

- **Crash:** `EEUGGather::FindGatherSpot` read `this->mResource` through a NULL `this` (c0000005, every time at
  105 minutes in one seed of boom_order against the improved classic). `EEUGBuildRepair::BeginRepair` asks the units on
  the site to step aside (`EEStepAsideFromSite`), and `EEComplexUnit::StepAside` takes a unit in
  `kActionWaitForOpenPosition` to have an `EEUGGather` goal: `dynamic_cast<EEUGGather*>(GetGoal())->FindGatherSpot`.
  This unit's goal was something else (probably a new order from a script, given while the action had not changed
  yet). Frames resolved from `EE-SIM.map` by address (the image loads at its preferred base).
- **Fix:** a NULL cast skips the gather-spot search; the unit stays where it is.

## The mouse pointer's save-under under GX (full screen, 2026-11-12)

- **Symptom**: in full screen (not windowed), moving the mouse left white squares and pieces of the pointer along its
  path, over the menus (Game Setup) and the game's top and bottom bars: everywhere the UI is redrawn only where it
  is dirty. The 3D view, redrawn every frame, hid them. The harness never saw it: its build is windowed.
- **Two save-unders, a DirectDraw flip chain behind them.** RTSMouse keeps two save-under records and swaps them every
  pointer frame. The graphics thread saves under the pointer, draws it, shows the frame and restores: windowed the
  record it just saved (the back buffer keeps its pixels after the blit to the window), in full screen the previous
  one, because a flip hands back the frame before last with the previous pointer in it. GX's Flip presents a copy of
  the back buffer and keeps it, so that full-screen restore put back a stale rectangle: the pointer drawn this frame
  stayed until the next one, and the next save took pieces of it in (the fragments).
- **The mouse-pointer thread draws on the primary.** Every 25 ms, when the pointer moved, RTSMousePointer restores,
  saves under and draws the pointer straight onto the screen (the original's pointer between frames), with the same
  records. GX's primary has no texture and sampling it gives white, so its save-under was white; the graphics
  thread's full-screen restore of "the previous record" then wrote that white rectangle into the back buffer.
- **Fix**: RTSGraphics::Render restores the frame's own record in full screen too (the windowed restore), and a GX
  blit from the primary reads what the window shows (the window image with the pointer's partial blits, else the last
  whole frame, in its coordinates) instead of white; in full screen, where Flip leaves no such frame, it leaves the
  target alone. Evidence, from a throwaway build that dumped the presented GPU copy and moved the pointer a little
  every frame (full-screen Game Setup, WARP): before, 2,517 graphics-thread restores of a pointer-thread record and
  3,125 white 8x8 blocks after 17,600 frames; after, none in full screen or windowed.
- **Not a regression of a recent commit**: both halves date from the GX renderer (2026-11-04). The harness and
  windowed play never show it, and how often the pointer thread runs between two frames depends on timing.
- Dumping a frame by setting the surface's CPU copy valid changes which path later blits take (CPU blits instead of
  GPU ones), and that hid the bug: dump frames without changing a surface's CPU/GPU state, or the evidence lies.
- The harness cannot see this class of bug: the test profile is windowed and the gates check milestones. A
  full-screen check needs a display. A disconnected session (this machine's RDP) still renders (WARP), but a BitBlt
  of the screen captures white.

## R5b.2, eleventh round: the stats reads from the stats table, the goals' last reads in Rust (ee_combat store.rs, reads.rs; branch rust-combat11, 2026-11-13)

Measured by net C++ deletion (src and include/ee, git numstat).

| Commit | What | C++ |
|---|---|---|
| the stats reads | the trigger, step and heal-work records' stats fields, the reads' seven stats cases, the damage record's armour from ee_units' stats table | +7 -45, net -38 |
| the goals' reads | `EECombatFillCondition` folded into `EECombatCondition(kind, unit, event, target, goal, class)` (six call sites one line each); `EEUGAttackUnit::IsGateClosed`/`IsStillReachable` and `EEUGHealUnit::IsInRange` deleted | +58 -91, net -33 |

  bridge `ee_combat_store_stats_of` copies the fields combat reads from `ee_units::stats::stats_of` (a Rust-to-Rust
  bridge: listed in cbindgen.toml's `exclude` with the other two, or it lands in `ee_rust_common.h` and makes that
  header include `ee_combat.h`). No stats object, or one the table lacks, reads 0 (the fills' NULL test); the
  original's reads dereferenced the stats unchecked, so no defined behaviour changed. The armour is a read
