## R6: the game screens, thirteenth round: the message box, the UI manager's factories, the framed background and the UI thread's action queues in Rust (ee_screens dialog.rs, factories.rs, frame.rs, actions.rs; branch rust-screens13, 2026-11-12)

The dialogs, the UI manager and the UI thread (RUST_PLAN's row: ~4.2k); round 10's count (`build/sc10/count.sh`).

- **The message box** (`dialog.rs`): `EEUIFError`'s five `Display*` and `Open`'s five `Layout*` are one Rust plan per
  kind over `ee_screenscpp_dialog` (in `EEUIFError.cpp`: the host of a C++ class lives with it, not in
  `EEScreens.cpp`, so a driver over the unit alone relinks). The box's statics hold `Display`'s inputs (message,
  data, callbacks, close form) for the length of the call; callbacks never cross into Rust (a slot number says
  which). The layouts' fractions travel as integers (`451 | 573 << 16`): the host's `451 / 1024.0f` is the same float
  as the original's constant. `LayoutMessage`'s centring is Rust's (`UMFloor` to a 32-bit `long`, the lines an
  unsigned 32-bit count as on Windows). The form, its controls and their construction, the buttons' drawing and
  `Close`'s posted callback stay C++. 38,083 -> 37,891 (-192; git over the C++ +139 -331).
- **The factories** (`factories.rs`): the twelve control-event factories `EEUIManager` registered one per form are
  one Rust table in their registration order (the toolkit takes the first answer that is not NULL, so the chain's
  order is the original's) behind one registered `EECreateGameEvent`; WON's server select factory stays C++ and is
  registered after it (the debug sound panel's, registered after WON's in the original, answers no id WON's does).
  The form-event factory is a Rust table. Events still C++ classes (the save/load Cancel, the unit reload, WON's
  server select open) are `EE_SCREENS_CPP_*` codes the C++ factory turns into its `new`s. 37,891 -> 37,588 (-303;
  git over the C++ +38 -341). The driver relinked prints the same for every id below 70,000.
- **The framed background** (`frame.rs`): `EEUIBGenericBackground`'s draw (the panel, edges, corners, side
  ornaments) is Rust's geometry over two host calls, the panel and one piece; a piece carries its texture and
  destination rectangles, location, cell and up to three reorders of the texture coordinates (each the new corners'
  indices into the current ones, two bits each), the scales swapped after a quarter turn. ee_screens now takes ee_ge
  for `GERectangle`'s `And` (a `GERectangle*` crosses as `void*`: ee_ge's `GeRectangle` is its layout, bottom first).
  Found by its unit test, the original's: a redraw rectangle that misses the background leaves the background's
  visible part whole (`And` in place does not touch it), so every piece is still drawn, clipped to the whole
  background. 37,588 -> 37,385 (-203; git over the C++ +42 -245). Only a tour draws it (39 generic backgrounds in
  `dbuiback`: the main game form's seven, the settings', the splash's, the lobby's; flags 1, 3 and 0, one form 5).
- **The action queues** (`actions.rs`): `EEUserInterface`'s action, undo and redo deques and their three critical
  sections are a Rust record of three `Mutex<VecDeque>`s of handles; the actions stay C++ (`EEAction`, reference
  counted) behind `ee_screenscpp_action` (reference, release, run, undo, undoable, the two locks). A pop releases the
  queue's mutex before the action is released or run (the original's `ClearQueue` released under its recursive
  critical section; an action's dtor that posts would deadlock a Rust mutex). 37,385 -> 37,311 (-74; git over the
  C++ +58 -145, `EEUserInterface.h` outside the count). The tour's orders, the gates' games and EE-SIM run every
  action through it (the oracle identical); the editor's Undo and Redo are a person's.
- **Round total:** game UI C++ lines 38,083 -> 37,311 (-772).
- **Golden drivers** (scratch, `build/sc13`: `dlg_driver.cpp`, `fac_driver.cpp`, `frm_driver.cpp`, `act_driver.cpp`;
  `drv.py` as round 12's): each runs the unmodified unit, then the new unit with the host renamed by a macro
  (`#define ee_screenscpp_dialog ee_screenscpp_dialog_real` before the `#include`) so the driver's own
  `ee_screenscpp_dialog` logs every host call and answer before forwarding. That log is the committed golden; the
  Rust replay checks each call against it and gives its answer (no toolkit model in Rust).
- **Lessons:**
  - A driver that names pointers must keep every named buffer alive: a callback's data pointer from an earlier case
    named a freed edit box line whose address the next case's line reused in one build and not the other (22 lines
    of a 62,000-line diff); the old and new units were the same.
  - A virtual member called on the driver's calloc'ed object goes through the fake vtable to a stub: call
    `p->Class::Open()` qualified (the first old run printed no layout at all).
  - Private `const`s of a module are exported by cbindgen too: `HIDDEN`/`SHOWN` landed in `ee_rust_common.h` and took
    `ee_ui`'s `SHOWN`. Prefix even private consts.
  - An env var holding `/DNAME` is rewritten by MSYS into a path when bash starts a Windows program: pass `-DNAME`.
  - ee_plat_core's timer tests fail under the machine's load in the workspace run (three different tests over three
    runs) and pass alone; the gate's `cargo test --workspace` stops at that crate, so `build/sc13/gate.sh` runs the
    gate's four steps with `--no-fail-fast` to see every other crate.
  - The main checkout's oracle ref can change under a running round: the lead re-recorded it (`rust` merged main's
    AI changes, a declared rebaseline) while this round's last commit ran, and the commit "diverged" at CT 744. Before
    chasing a divergence, check the ref's time against the branch's base; this branch matched `ref_pre_mm2`, the ref
    of its base, identically (trace and ticks), and the merged branch matches the new ref.
- **Not moved:** the UI thread's message loop and handlers (`EEUserInterface::HandleMessage` and the game-state
  transitions it calls: one world, server or graphics call per line; a Rust move adds a host op per line and deletes
  nothing until the simulation interface of step (3)), `EEUIManager::CreateUserDefinedControl` (the HUD's controls by
  kind) and `StartScenarioEditor`, `EEUIFileComboBox` (a toolkit control subclass). The scenario editor's map is in
  RUST_PLAN's row.

## R6 WON round 24: MultiListArea with its rows and header, TreeArea and TreeItem, PopupMenu whole in Rust; the lists' selection event fixed (ee_won multiobj.rs, treeobj.rs, menuobj.rs; branch rust-r6-won24, 2026-11-13)

Measured as rounds 18-23 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi`, `wc -l`): 87,629 at
the branch's start -> 87,632 (MultiListArea accessors, +3) -> 86,904 (the multi-column list, -728) -> 86,908 (TreeItem
accessors, +4) -> 86,252 (the tree, -656) -> 86,100 (PopupMenu, -152); the merge of rust (other lanes) -> 85,300;
the selection event fix +5, the Scrollbar accessors +13 -> 85,318. This round's own net: -1,511.

- **The regression (found by the lead's LAN gate, fixed here in its own commit):** round 23's Rust ListArea fires its
  selection change through the component op `FireEvent(EeWonGuiEvent::ListSelChanged)`, and GuiHost's `ComponentOp`
  turned every event but InputReturn into `ComponentEvent_InputTextChanged`. No list's selection reached a listener,
  so the LAN lobby never enabled Join Game. The golden could not see it: its host traced the op, not the event the
  C++ made of it. Lesson: when an op's C++ side maps codes, check each code reaches its own case (a new code added to
  a shared op table needs its host case too).
- **Accessors first, in their own commits.** MultiListArea: the configs' and ServerListCtrl's writes of
  `mDynamicSizeColumn` / `mAutoGrowColumns` and read of `mSortColumnPrev`. TreeItem: RoomCtrl's reads of `mItem`,
  `mChildren.size()`, `mParent`, `mIndex`, `mOpen` (`GetWrappedItem`, `GetNumChildren`, `GetParentItem`, `GetIndex`,
  `IsOpen`). Scrollbar: the skins, MSScrollbar, the configs and ScrollbarScroller (arrows, thumb, track, orientation,
  thumb options, `SetRange`, `SetLineScrollSizes`, `Get/SetPosition`); the move itself is next round. PopupMenu had no
  reader outside its units.
- **Subclasses over a Rust base.** MultiListArea, TreeArea and PopupMenu derive from ListArea, which is Rust since
  round 23. Their Rust objects hold the list's Rust object (`ee_won_*_new(this, host, this->mRust)`: the base's
  constructor ran first and its destructor runs after) and call it directly for every `ListArea::X` the original
  made. The list's own virtuals (AdjustPosition, Sort, NotifyMouseItemGone, ListSelChangedHook) still go back through
  the C++ object, so the overrides run. The goldens run BOTH sides over a real Rust ListArea with one scripted host,
  so the traces carry the base's ops too.
- **Rows as Rust objects.** MultiListItem and TreeItem stay C++ `ListItem`s (the list's items; NetworkAdapterListItem
  derives from MultiListItem), each holding a Rust row (`EeWonMRow`, `EeWonTNode`) with its cells or its children
  and wrapped item held by reference. A row's virtuals get the list, and the forwarder passes along the list's Rust
  object. The calls with no list (`SetPos`, `GetItem`, the walks) go through the row's own small host (references,
  `NodeOf`, the item SetPos). A row reaches another row's Rust state through the op `NodeOf` (the C++ row's `mNode`),
  and the header reaches its list's through `MultiOf`.
- **Undefined states the goldens avoid (the Rust keeps away from them):**
  - a negative column to `SetItem` / `SetColumnItem` (the original compared it with the vector's size as unsigned);
  - a row's cell past the columns at paint (the original read past the vector);
  - a header without a list at a drag (a null read).
  - In the tree, `CloseAll` alone, or a changing call on a hidden row left open, can leave rows of a closed or
    detached subtree in the list. Their parent's removal then makes the original read a freed row (the first tree
    golden crashed there). The tree golden's changing calls take shown rows, as the room control does.
- **Unset fields given a value:** TreeArea's `mTreeSortType` (none; the config sets it) and PopupMenu's
  `mLastX`/`mLastY` (0; only keyboard mode reads them, after a move set them). One dropped override:
  `TreeArea::MouseDown` only called `ListArea::MouseDown`.
- **The tree's paint** is guidraw's operations. The dotted lines' pixel loops are a new `EE_WON_DRAW_DOTTED_LINE`
  (17), executed by `WONDrawOne`.
- **The sorts:** a row's Compare is called from `std::sort` / `std::lower_bound` inside the list's ops. The goldens'
  hosts sort through the side's rows. The Rust replays take a sort's order from the golden and run `lower_bound`'s
  binary search themselves (the same comparisons).
- **The goldens** (`tests/won/won_multiobj_test.cpp`, `won_treeobj_test.cpp`, `won_menuobj_test.cpp`; 20,000
  sequences each, every reference given back):

  | Golden | Trace lines | Mutation | Sequences it fails | Replayed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | multi-column list | 11,327,345 | an empty cell's order | 4,342 | 46 sequences |
  | tree | 13,409,107 | an ancestor's dotted line's x | 3,014 | 42 sequences |
  | popup menu | 6,174,909 | the cleared submenu selection's index | 2,337 | 40 sequences |

  `WON_TRACE_SEQ` / `WON_ECHO` / `WON_FIRST_SEQ` in the tree test print the sequence and its live trace (how its
  crash was found).
- **Shell lesson:** the Bash tool turned `\n` inside a heredoc into a real newline, even with a quoted delimiter. It
  broke a C string literal twice: write such files with the file tool.
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby (the oracle is unchanged by construction). The lead's LAN game
  checks:
  - the LAN game list (a plain ListArea) and its selection event (`lan_game.py` PASS here, after the fix);
  - the game room's player list (MultiListArea: GameUserListCtrl's rows over MultiListItem);
  - the right-click menus (PopupMenu) if a person opens one.

  The tree is the Internet room list only. The lobby captures check the multi-column paint (rows, columns, header
  buttons, sort arrows). Column drags, header sorts, submenus, keyboard menus and the tree's mouse run only in the
  goldens.
- **Left:** Scrollbar (accessors done) with ScrollbarScroller; TextListItem and MenuItem's paints (data classes the
  lobby fills; their decisions are guidraw's); then the containers.

## R5b.4, seventeenth round: EEUGRust generic over the goal kind; the cast calamity, explore and unload transport goals whole in Rust (ee_units rust_goal.rs, calamity.rs, explore.rs, unload.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core17, 2026-11-13)

- **One host for every Rust goal: an operation callback, not a table.** Round 16's `EEUGRust` had the patrol's
  21-function host table; a second class would have needed its own and cost as much as it saved. The class is now
  generic: every virtual calls `ee_units_rust_goal(op, kind, goal, a, b, io, host)`, which dispatches by `mKind` to
  the class's bodies, and the C++ answers through one callback (`EeUnitsGoalHost`: an operation number, two handles
  and an argument block of ints, floats, a text and a list sink). Each read or world call is one `case` of a switch
  (two to five lines) instead of a function plus a table entry. Rust keeps one trait per class (`PatrolHost`,
  `CalamityHost`, `ExploreHost`, `UnloadHost`, over a common `GoalHost`), so the bodies and their mock-host tests
  stay typed; one adapter (`OpHost`) implements them all over the callback.
- **The texts and the defaults moved with it.** The debug line and text and the out-of-synch dump are Rust
  (`format!`, appended through the host into the `UWideString` or the dump's `FILE`; a unit's class name is its own
  operation); `GetDestination` with its group notice, `GetStartAction`, `Start`, the base `EvaluateCondition`,
  `GetMaxPathAttempts` (3, the unload's 9) and `Suits` (true, the unload's test) are answered in Rust, and `Load` and
  `RepairPointers` hand Rust the save version. A class moved later adds only its own operations and accessors.
- **What it deleted.** C++ (src and include, not the generated header) per commit: the cast calamity with the
  generic rework +392 -738 (net -346), explore +197 -470 (-273), unload transport +213 -511 (-298): the round -917
  before the merge, against the lane's +83 over rounds 15-16.
- **Explore's bad tiles are ee_astar's `SparseArray`** (ee_units now depends on ee_astar and ee_ge): the point set
  behind `U2DSparseArrayPointContainer` was already Rust, so the save lists the bad tiles in the same order and the
  checksum's count is its `size`. `GE3DPoint::DistanceToSquared` is ee_ge's.
- **State by value, no lock across a host call.** Each body copies its goal's record out of the table, calls the
  host, and writes it back (the explore record, with its point set, is cloned). A reentrant body for the same goal
  would see the record as it was before the outer body; no gate game has one.
- **Two unit types behind one handle.** A goal's target may be any `EEUnit` while its source or transport is an
  `EEComplexUnit`; single inheritance puts both at the same address, so the host casts each handle to the type the
  original read through, and the saved ids' lookup says which (`find_unit(id, complex)`).
- **Accessors for the callers' member reads.** The AI read and wrote the classes' members directly: the prophet the
  cast's technology, tile and target; the active group the explore copy's tile and the unload's tile; the AI
  personnel the unload's destination before `FindUnloadTiles` (now `SetUnloadDestination`, one call); the air
  bomber cleared the transport so the goal's destructor would not release it (`ForgetUnloadTransport`). The
  compiler lists them once the class is gone.
- **Coverage by temporary prints (removed).** No game of any profile reaches the cast calamity goal (calamity seeds
  2-7; oracle, late, space, missile, scenario 2-3: the calamity profile's calamities are cast through the manager)

  hands the kinds it does not own to one function ee_rust registers in `ee_rust_init`
  (`register_other_goal_kinds`); ee_combat mirrors `EeUnitsGoalIo` and `EeUnitsGoalHost` and ee_rust asserts the
  layouts and the copied operation numbers at compile time. The combat host operations (from 1000) are the C++
  host's `default:` case (`EECombatGoalHostOp`). The generic part gained one virtual (`SetPathAttempts`: the attack
  goal's 0 clears its sidestep count) and one public wrapper of its `Goal` call for accessors outside EEUGRust.cpp.

  by one in a capture of oracle seed 2 and an oracle-mode run of seed 3).

  oracle then failed for the unmodified parent build too. A baseline run of the parent exe (kept as a copy before

  `mCombatState`) then counted hunts, and the AI's combat state changed the game at 59 s. Read the enum, not memory
  (ee_units has a test that checks its copies against the headers; ee_combat's goal constants have none yet).

  on some paths, so the attack's GetDestination takes the caller's point in and out (`io.f`), as the original's
  reference did.

  the first byte): compare saves by their continuation (saveload), not by bytes.

  same at any version, but the attack goal writes its live state only for a version that has it, while Load reads by
  the file's version: every load of a game with an attack goal read past the record (EE-SIM fault in
  `QueueLoadGoal`). Save now hands the body the version, as Load and RepairPointers do. The oracle and the captures

## R5b.4, eighteenth round: the herd's continent after a load; the load goals whole in Rust; EEUGLocation's accessors (ee_units load.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core18, 2026-11-13)

| Commit | What | C++ |
|---|---|---|
| e82b9142 | a loaded herd keeps its saved continent | +5 -2 |
| 530ab345 | saveload_expect: oracle seed 2 at 1000 s END | (tool) |
| fff5f63f | cherry-pick of combat's 2e5e35a1: EEUGRust::Save hands the version | +1 -1 |
| e5abdb28 | the load goals whole in Rust (EEUGLoadContainer, EEUGLoadGarrison, EEUGLoadTransport deleted) | +350 -1484, net -1134 |
| 5e1f9035 | EEUGLocation's accessors, its members protected | +70 -60 |

- **The save gap was not the mine list.** The main merge's note blamed `mMines` (27 entries after a load, 8 in the
  continued game). That difference is real: the load's `RefreshResourceCenters` rebuilds the list, and the unit
  manager's citizen target reads it (`GetGatherCapacity`) before the resource manager's first `Update` takes the saved
  one. Making `Refresh` take the saved lists at the load closed it, but no save in 40 (plains, islands, mediterranean,
  medium difficulty, seeds 2-3 at 1000/1900 s) changed, so that change was not committed. The first difference was found by
  `--dump-at` at the parting tick in both games, then a temporary `fprintf` with `__builtin_return_address(0)`
  resolved against `EE-SIM.map` (the image loads at its preferred base): a newborn animal's goal came from
  `EEHerd::GiveGoal`, and the two games put it in different herds. `EEHerd::CanTake` compares the herd's
  `mContinent`, saved, but `RepairPointers` recomputed it from the first animal's tile at the load, and a leaving
  herd's first animal had crossed to another continent. A 0.263 save (its regions restored) now keeps the saved value:
  oracle seed 2's 1000 s save continues to the end. No other row of the matrix changed (plains-medium-3ai, islands,
  mediterranean, medium-difficulty, late, space and next still part where they did).
- **The load goals on the generic EEUGRust.** The same pattern as round 17: one Rust record per goal object
  (`load.rs`), one host operation per world call (20 new cases; the unload's sound case now falls through into a
  generic sound case). The C++ keeps the caller's list sort (`std::sort` by `mUnitID`, `std::unique`): the callers then
  walk the sorted list, so the sort must still happen in place in the caller's vector. `EeUnitsGoalIo` gained a handle
  list (`list`, `list_len`: the rendezvous search's units) and eight floats (the boarding search's location and result);
  the file calls gained a `float` type (3).
- **The base goal's defaults bite.** The first oracle run parted at seed 3's tick 358: a town building upgraded by its
  garrison (`EEReplaceUnit`) idled in the original and stayed in `GarrisonUpgrade` here. `EEUGLoadContainer::Suits`
  answered true, as `EEUGRust`'s dispatch did for the other kinds, but the load kinds were excluded from that default
  (to answer 6 path attempts) and their body fell through to 0. A kind that leaves the generic defaults must answer
  every one of them itself. The diagnosis: the base exe rebuilt from a stash with a print in the garrison constructor,
  and a comparison of both exes' dumps.
- **Uninitialized fields.** The garrison's list constructor never set `mCost` or `mUpgrade` for a goal whose upgrade is
  unavailable (and the AI queues such goals without testing `mIsValid`). Rust starts them at 0. No gate game made one.
- **Coverage by a temporary print (removed).** Garrison goals run in every random-map game: oracle and late seeds 2-3
  (creation, copies, steps, triggers, destination, abandon, the replacement on upgrade, destruction). Transport goals
  run only in the saveload games (islands, late, space): creation, start, steps, triggers, and the AI's reads of the
  unit list. No game saves or loads a load goal (`Save`, `Load`, `RepairPointers`: unit tests only), and the scenario
  profile reaches neither kind.
- **EEUGLocation's accessors.** Making the members `protected` (not private: `EEUGHealUnit` derives from the class)
  let the compiler list every outside access. `build.py --compile-only` reports a file's errors only up to clang's
  limit and then moves on, so it took four passes. A script turned each named column into the accessor (assignments
  into the setter).
- **Process lessons.**
  - A `git commit` after a `git rm` commits the staged deletions with the file you meant to commit. `git add` the one
    file is not enough; check `git status` (repaired here by a soft reset before anything else).
  - Bash heredocs turned `\n` in a Python string into a real newline three times. Write such scripts with the file
    tool.
  - The open tree's `Data/ai` changed under the main checkout's `ref` mid-round (folder hash 327d5891 -> 1494ba43):
    the oracle "parted" at line 0. Compare against a ref made by the branch's base exe on the same tree.
- **Gates.** Per commit: build `--sim` 0/0, oracle seeds 2-3 identical, Rust gate PASS (the load commit). Captures at
  seeds 2-3: oracle, late, scenario PASS. Saveload: the full matrix on e82b9142 as the expect file (one row better);
  oracle, islands, late and space at seeds 2-3 on the load tree as the expect file.

## R4.4, ninth round: the weather storms, the 3D icons, the energy walls and the tracer beams on the records (ee_gfx effect_storm.rs, effect_icon.rs, effect_wall.rs, effect_tracer.rs; branch rust-gfx15, 2026-11-12)

More effect leaf families on the round-7 records, one family a commit, largest first, EFST the gate (seeds 2-3 of the
oracle and late profiles per commit, calamity too for the storms, which a hurricane makes). Graphics Thread C++
(`src/Empire Earth/Graphics Thread/*.cpp`): 24,878 lines before the round, 24,188 after it (storms -522, icons -56,
energy walls -93, tracer beams -19).

- **The weather storms** (`EEE3DStorm`, `EEE3DRain`, `EEE3DSnow`: `EeGfxEffectStorm`). The tiles and the drops (the
  rain's drops and the snow's flakes, one Rust type) are a Rust value the record owns (`EeGfxStormLists`, made on
  first use, freed with the record, taken out of it for each call like the damage controller's children). In Rust:
  the constructor's tiles; `GetCenter` (the mean divided as unsigned); `Move` (each tile one step towards its place
  around the new centre through `EEGetTileDirection`/`EEGetNextTile`, kept where that tile is off the map; the bounds
  start at the old centre; the radius from the integer half sides); `GetBounds`; the one `SetUp` of both leaves (the
  float mean, the radius to the farthest tile in x or y); the spawn (the tile, x and y draws, then the flake's two
  drift draws); the update (the target count's ramp with the original's unsigned `target - count + extra` and its
  sign flip, at most 65 new drops a tick and none above 1400; the rain's fall and its one-in-16 ripple draw on
  landing, made before the water test; the snow's fall by the tick over the game speed, its spin and its 5% drift
  turn); the age and the end (the snow waits for its last flake); the rain's thunder timer (`StartSounds`' two draws);
  the respawn after a load; Load and Save by kind (the rain's thunder delay between the count and the discarded
  position). The C++ keeps the sounds, the models, the draws and the world (tiles, terrain heights, the land ripple,
  the next-tile helpers: `EeGfxStormHost`). `Queue` copies the drops into a C++ vector of `EeGfxStormDraw` for the
  draw pass, which runs without the lock while the tick steps the drops, as the original's copy did: the draw never
  reads the Rust list. `EEEMStorm` reads the centre and the tile count through `GetCenterPoint`/`GetTileCount`; the
  leaves' `Queue`, `SetUp`, `Load`, `Save`, `RepairPointers` and the snow's `Step` became the storm's; `EE3DRainDrop`,
  `EE3DRainDraw`, `EEE3DSnowFlake`, `EE3DSnowDraw`, `mL74` and `EEE3DStorm.cpp`'s unused file-static tile map are gone.

## R4.4, tenth round: the effect manager's algorithms, the capture's fade, letterbox, clocks and daylight blend and its per-object arithmetic in Rust (ee_gfx effect_manager.rs, scene.rs, capture.rs; branch rust-gfx16, 2026-11-12)

Round 9 found the effect leaves yielding under 0.5k lines a round, so this round took the larger structures. Graphics
Thread C++ (`src/Empire Earth/Graphics Thread/*.cpp`): 24,188 lines before the round; 23,699 after the manager
(`EEEffectManager.cpp` 1,162 -> 673); 23,573 after the capture's state and arithmetic (`EERenderObject.cpp`
2,026 -> 1,900).

- **The effect manager (`effect_manager.rs`, `ffi_manager.rs`).** Over the round-6 store: the creation plan of each
  of the eight entry points (`CreateUnitEffect` ... `CreateWeatherEffect`: above the detail setting nothing and 0;
  a kind the entry does not make 10, but 0 for `CreateEffectBetween` and `CreateWeatherEffect`; a kind without the
  living (complex) unit or units it needs 10; the multi-effect unsaved), the registration (unsaved first, `SetUp`,
  `AddEffect` under a new handle even when the set-up fails, the handle out; a pool that returns no effect gives 0),
  `AddEffect`, `RemoveEffect`, `DestroyQueued` (its 3/9 result), `ClearEffects`, `RepairPointers`' walk (7 or above
  the detail setting: dropped; another error stops it; then the goal markers'), `Load` (the counter, the effects by
  kind, a save before 0.200 giving handles anew, an effect added even when its load fails, the goal markers, the
  queue), `Save` (an effect's error can be overwritten by the next one's, as the original) and `Update`'s loop. The
  effects stay C++ objects: the C++ constructs them per entry point (one switch each, without the unit tests) and
  per saved kind, and answers `EeGfxEffectManagerHost` (record, reference, release, set-up, step, repair, the
  detail test, the load-time constructor, load, save, the goal markers). Every call is the original's in its order:
  an effect the update or the queue removes is released twice, as before. The store is borrowed for one operation
  at a time (`StoreAccess::with`), never across a callback: a step, a set-up or a load creates and destroys effects
  in between. `AddEffect`, `RemoveEffect` and `DestroyQueued` left the class (nothing else called them). One
  difference: `Load`'s handle counter was an uninitialized local in the original (garbage in the store after a
  failed first read); it starts at 0. Verified by the EFMU and EFST capture records (recorded from the C++ manager
  in rounds 6 and 7) in the oracle, late and calamity profiles and by unit tests with a mock host (the call log of
  update, queue, repair and clear; save and load round trips; old saves; errors). No golden driver over the original

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 14 (the certificate classes, AuthPeerData, the peer authentication and its ops as Rust objects)

Branch `rust-won-net14`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 13. The set moved as one because the hooks
cross: the handshake's environment was the certificates and the peer data, the ops held the handshake.

- **What moved.** `peerobj.rs`: `Cert` (AuthBase with AuthCertificate, Auth2Certificate and AuthPubKeyBlock: the
  bytes, the unpacked block, its keys), `PeerData` (AuthPeerData: the certificates, the key block, the private
  key, the clock delta) and `PeerAuth` (PeerAuthClient / PeerAuthServer: the handshake's state, the peer data, both
  secrets, the other side's certificate, the session it makes), the handshake's `PeerEnv` the original's `Pa*`
  statements over them. `peerop.rs`: PeerAuthOp and PeerAuthServerOp on the op base, every step. The C++ left:
  `AuthBase` / `AuthPeerData` RefCount shims (WONAuthPeerData.h; one reference each, read by number), and
  PeerAuthOp / PeerAuthServerOp as RustServerOps (constructors in ServerOp.cpp, `GetSession`,
  `GetGetCertStatus`, `ClientPermits`). Ten units and three headers deleted; WONPeerAuthMsg.h moved to
  `tests/won/won_peerauth_msg.h`. src+include: +155 -944 (the objects), +52 -574 (the ops).
- **Random draws are part of the behaviour.** Every `ElGamal()` the original constructed seeded a generator from
  the system seed, including keys it threw away at once (a certificate's member key before the unpacking replaced
  it, the one `Adopt(NULL)` made, a key block's `ElGamal key;` per key, an empty peer data's private key). With a
  fixed seed (`ee_won_random_test_seed`) the secrets and encryptions only match when the Rust objects draw at the
  same points, so they do (a dropped `ElGamal::new()` where the original discarded one).
- **The system seed's counter is per thread in the crate's tests.** Parallel tests shared the global counter, so
  a replay that fixes the seed could not be deterministic (round 12 avoided it by injecting generators). Under
  `cfg(test)` the counter and the fixed base are thread-locals; the game and the drivers keep the globals.
- **Small keys do not encrypt.** auth.rs's 30-bit test group signs and verifies, but its encryption gives NULL
  (not investigated); the goldens use four keys over a 192-bit group, made once with
  ee_won's bigint and kept as constants in both the driver and the replay.
- **A golden whose answers are recorded replays an op without porting its stand-in.** `golden_peerop.txt` writes
  every call with its answer (`recv(o1000,60003)=0:<bytes>`); the Rust replay answers from the line and checks
  each call against it. Only the other end of the socket (a real handshake, whose draws interleave with the op's)
  runs again in the replay. Member reads (mode, times, auth type) are answered but not logged, so the argument
  order of `QueueOp(Track(new op), SendTime())` does not show.
- **Stable times.** Certificates expire in 2037 or in 1970 and clock deltas cross that or not, so the goldens
  hold for years; "expires within 120 seconds but not 30" (AsyncRun's refresh that still connects) needs times
  relative to now and is not covered.
- **Goldens first.** `won_peerobj_test` (600 scenarios in `golden_peerobj.txt`; 3,000 run, the game's classes
  against won_auth_orig.h's copies, 0 failed; a mutation fails 461) and `won_peerop_test` (500 sequences in
  `golden_peerop.txt`; 2,000 run, the Rust ops against the original's statements, 0 failed; a mutation fails 205).
- **The original's undefined corners, defined.** A NULL second certificate (IsValid2, Certificate2Expired, the
  server's own raw certificate, LanLogic's first community) is invalid, expired, empty, 0; a key block with no key
  encrypts nothing; PeerAuthOp's refresh status the constructor left unset is 0; a NULL received message is
  empty; a handshake step that succeeds with nothing to send sends an empty message; the server's `Success` with
  no session finishes without encryption.
- **Which LAN paths reach it.** The LAN lobby makes an AuthContext, so `new AuthPeerData` (the Rust empty peer
  data) runs in every LAN session. The peer authentication runs only for a direct-connect game (type 3) with the
  CD key check on: the host's `LanStartPeerAuth` (a PeerAuthServerOp on each accepted socket, then
  `HandlePeerAuthDone`'s `ClientPermits`) and the joiner's `LanConnect` with peer auth (a PeerAuthOp,
  AUTH_TYPE_PERSISTENT); both first need `LanRefreshCertificate`, a GetCertOp from the WON servers, which are
  gone, so the gate's LAN game (a LAN-listed game) does not reach them. The Internet login reaches the rest
  (ServerConnection's connect, a request's peer authentication, GetCertOp's certificates).
- **Not moved, and why.** AuthContext's peer data stays a C++ `ConstSmartPtr<AuthPeerData>` (a shim now) and its
  four flow hooks (`CertPeerData`, `LightSetPeerData`, `PeerValid`, `PeerExpireDelta`) stay: they are one call
  each into the Rust object, and moving the member into authflow.rs means re-recording golden_authflow.txt's hook
  vocabulary. LightGetCertOp stays a C++ AsyncOp (the auth context's refresh queue holds it).

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 15 (AuthContext's peer data and LightGetCertOp's member in authflow.rs)

Branch `rust-won-net15`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 14. The servers are gone: an Internet login
and a direct-connect LAN game with the CD key check reach this code; the drivers and the Rust replays exercise it.

- **What moved.** `authflow.rs`'s `EeWonAuthFlow` owns the context's peer data now (`mPeerData`, peerobj.rs's
  `PeerData` in an `Arc`): `GetPeerData` (a fresh `AuthPeerData` shim over a new reference,
  `AuthPeerData::Adopt`), `SetPeerData` (the replacement and the session clear in one call), `IsExpired` and the
  auto-refresh's reads of the validity and expire delta. `LightGetCertOp`'s member (the peer data
  `GetCertCallback` hands each waiting op) is `EeWonLightCert`, shared by the refresh set and the PeerAuthOp that
  made it; the op's run is a plain C++ `AsyncOp` (`new AsyncOp` for `EE_WON_HOST_PEER_NEW_LIGHT`), the C++ class
  `LightGetCertOp` is deleted. Three of the four flow hooks are gone (`LightSetPeerData`, `PeerValid`,
  `PeerExpireDelta`); `CertPeerData` stays (the GetCertOp's peer data is still a C++ shim the op's host calls
  make) and answers with a Rust reference. The host call `EE_WON_HOST_PEER_LIGHT_DATA` is gone: PeerAuthOp reads
  its light op's member. src+include +42 -49.
- **Time is a parameter.** The original's `GetExpireDelta` read `time(NULL)` inside; the flow's calls that can
  start the timer (`SetDoAutoRefresh`, `StartAutoRefresh`, `GetCertCallback`, `RefreshBlock`) take `now`, and
  `AuthContext` passes `time(NULL)`. The drivers pass a fixed certificates' clock, so a golden made of real
  certificates never ages.
- **Real peer data in the goldens, stand-ins beside them.** The original's half keeps its stand-in peer data
  (valid or not, a fixed expire delta). The Rust half gets real peer data: a valid one is a certificate and key
  block over the test key (signature checks are not part of `IsValid`: a block is valid when it parses and has
  bytes left for a signature) with the private key, its clock delta chosen so that its expire delta at the fixed
  clock is the stand-in's. An expired one answers 0 where the stand-in answered its negative delta: the auto-refresh
  wait is `max(delta - 120, 120)`, the same for both.
- **The vocabulary changed, the scripts did not.** golden_authflow.txt re-recorded with the same seed: the reads
  of the context's peer data (`valid:`, `delta:`) and the waiting ops' `setpeer:` are no calls out any more and
  are gone; a waiting op's peer data is logged when it completes (`done:l3:0:p5`); peer data frees are not
  logged (an `Arc` on the Rust side). Normalized the same way, the old and new goldens differ only in the order of
  runs of frees that a dropped token used to split. golden_peerop.txt: `lightdata(o1)=p2` after the completion's
  callback became `lightpeer(o1)=p2` right after `done(o1)`, where the context's `GetCertCallback` sets it;
  identical otherwise.
- **Identity across the C ABI.** Peer data handed out is a new box per reference; `ee_won_authobj_same` compares
  the objects (the drivers name a light op's peer data with it).
- **Checks.** won_authctx_test 100,000 scripts, 2,644,851 checks, 0 failed (mutations: the expire delta off by
  one fails 23,994; the light ops' peer data dropped fails 16,366); won_peerop_test 2,000 sequences, 0 failed (the
  light peer data dropped fails 205). Cargo: authflow's golden, its unit tests and a new one for the peer data
  and the light member; peerop's golden.
- **LAN reach.** Every LAN session makes an AuthContext, so `Init`'s empty peer data now goes into the flow
  (`ee_won_peer_new_empty`, the same draws as `new AuthPeerData`). `GetPeerData` (LanLogic::HandlePeerAuthDone)
  and `IsExpired` (LanLogic::RefreshCertificate) run only for a direct-connect game with the CD key check on, as
  the light op (PeerAuthOp's certificate refresh); the gate's LAN game does not reach them.
- **Not moved, and why.** The rest of the "Left" list waits on the socket objects (the lobby lane's round 15):
  ServerRequestOp's object is the RustServerOp host answering the ops' socket calls; ServerConnection is a
  BlockingSocket; the routing ops run on a RoutingConnection (a ServerConnection); UDPManager is the lobby lane's;
  TitleConfig is a ConfigObject, still C++ (WONGUI's configs derive from it).

## R6 WON round 25: Scrollbar, Scroller with ScrollbarScroller and ScrollArea whole in Rust, the items' measure and the menu item's paint; the event type out of the C++ (ee_won barobj.rs, scrollerobj.rs, paneobj.rs, guidraw.rs; branch rust-r6-won25, 2026-11-13)

Measured as rounds 18-24 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi`, `wc -l`): 85,318 at
the branch's start (round 24 merged into rust) -> 85,319 (the scrollers' accessors, +1) -> 85,110 (Scrollbar, -209)
-> 84,995 (Scroller and ScrollbarScroller, -115) -> 84,957 (the items, -38) -> 84,962 (ScrollArea's accessors, +5)
-> 84,750 (ScrollArea, -212). This round's own net: -568; the merge of rust changed no WON line.

- **What listeners receive (round 24's lesson, applied).** `FireEvent`'s type is no longer a C++ switch:
  GuiHost fires `ee_won_gui_event_type(event)`, a Rust map from `EeWonGuiEvent` to `WindowEventType`, so a new
  event code needs no C++ case to be forgotten. The enum moved to its own header (`WONEventTypes.h`, which
  `WONLobbyGUI.h` includes) so the goldens can include it without the GUI: `won_barobj_test` checks every code's
  type against the original enum and traces each scroll event as the type the C++ delivers (`fire 16`), the
  original side firing `ComponentEvent_Scroll` from the enum. Mapping Scroll to 21 fails 18,992 of its
  sequences. The older goldens (input, list) still trace the op; their events go through the same map now.
- **Untraced reads.** The goldens of this round trace only what changes something (and what the C++ virtuals the
  ops call do); the pure reads (sizes, positions, the parent test, the disabled state, the event's type and
  component, the casts, an area's numbers) are answered from the host's model and not traced. Their order in the
  original is the compiler's argument evaluation (right to left for the Microsoft ABI), not the program's, so a
  traced read order would pin a platform. The Rust replays keep the same model from the goldens' driver lines.
- **Scrollbar** (`barobj.rs`): the four parts held by reference (the original's `SmartPtr` assignment: the old
  part released, then the new one held; released thumb, track, down, up at the end), the orientation, the thumb
  options (the minimum an `unsigned char`), range, steps, position and drag (its unset drag offsets are 0). The
  C++ class keeps only its vtable and forwarders; the skins, configs and scrollers reach the parts through the
  round 24 accessors, now forwarders. The splitter's and the bar's child ops share GuiHost's `ContainerOp`.
- **Scroller and ScrollbarScroller** (`scrollerobj.rs`): one Rust object the `Scroller` constructor makes (a plain
  Scroller never uses the bars), holding the scroll area and both bars by reference, the conditions (both Enable)
  and the flag of their application. A bar's own methods are called on its Rust object (op `BarOf`, as round
  24's `NodeOf`), its `SetEnabled` through the C++ virtual. The subclasses (MSScrollContainer, WONScrollContainer,
  MSListCtrl, WONListCtrl) and the predefined components read the bars and the area through `GetScrollbar` /
  `GetScrollArea` (an accessor commit first; MSScrollContainer's constructor sets them through `SetBar`, the
  field only, as it did).
- **ScrollArea** (`paneobj.rs`): offsets, content, the last adjusted numbers, the last view size, padding, the
  user's scroll, the scroller (borrowed, as the original), view, extra height and the scroll amounts. The
  viewport and the background stay C++ members. Every virtual the original called on itself (AdjustPosition,
  Virtual08, ScrollSizeChanged, ScrollPaint) goes through the C++ object, so ListArea's and TextArea's overrides
  run. The list's and text area's Rust objects keep their `Get` / `Set` field ops; GuiHost answers them from the
  area's Rust object (`GetField` / `SetField`; `FieldOf` deleted). AdjustPosition reads the numbers it records
  after the scroller's notification, as the original did: the notification can lay the area out again

## R6 WON round 26: Container, Dialog and ScrollAreaViewport whole in Rust (ee_won ctobj.rs, dialogobj.rs; branch rust-r6-won26, 2026-11-13)

Measured as rounds 18-25 (every file under `src/Empire Earth/WONAPI` and `include/ee/wonapi`, `wc -l`): 84,750 at
the branch's start (round 25's head) -> 84,768 (Container's accessors, +18) -> 84,160 (Container, -608) -> 84,053
(Dialog, -107) -> 83,977 (ScrollAreaViewport, -76). This round's own net: -773 (the accessors +18, the moves -791).

- **The census first** (its own commit). Outside the container's seven units the lobby and WONGUI read
  `mHasUsedDialogKeys` (the buttons' dialog keys and focus paints), `mFocusChild` / `mMouseChild` (ComboBox,
  DialogBehavior, GuiHost), `mCurrentCursor` (RootContainer's cursor component, `Window::CheckSetCursor`,
  GuiHost), `mIsolateTabFocus` (RootContainer), `mModalCount` (`Component::WantFocus`), and `mChildList` with
  `Component::mChildListItr` (`GetNextSibling`, RootContainer's top child, the test fixture's lobby walk,
  ScrollAreaViewport::Reset). Each became an accessor; `GetNextSibling` became the parent's `NextChild`.
- **The move** (`ctobj.rs`): the child list (each child held by reference), the mouse and focus children, the timer
  children (held, a `BTreeSet` of addresses: the original's `std::set<SmartPtr>` ordered by raw pointer), the next
  focus id, the current cursor (held: the `SmartPtr` assignment releases the old one before holding the new), the
  flags and the modal count, with every method of the seven units and `MouseAt`. The child layout manager stays
  C++, owned by pointer so it is still destroyed between the cursor and the timer children (the member order).
  `Component::mChildListItr` is gone: a child's node is found by its address (a child is in one list).
- **The list is a linked list of nodes, not a `Vec`.** The original iterates its `std::list` while calling
  children, and a callee may insert or remove siblings; each loop reads the next node after the call, as the
  original's `++i`, and an erased node keeps its links, so an iteration around a callee's change goes on as the
  original's did. (A `Vec` index would skip or repeat a child after a removal before it.)
- **Every call out is one of five shapes:** `CtBase` (`Component::X` on itself), `CtChild` (a child's virtual),
  `CtParentCall` (`mParent->X(this)`), `CtVirt` (its own virtual: FindChildAt, SetCursor, TabFocus, RemoveChild,
  MouseMove, so the subclasses' overrides run), with the virtual named by `EeWonCtVirt`; plus the setters and the
  pure reads (flags, parent, bounds, timer flags, invalid state, focus id, the root, the mouse, the sibling walk).
  The host (`Container.cpp`) is two switches over the virtual's name. A subclass object (the dialog) holds the
  container's Rust object and calls it directly for `Container::X`.
- **Behaviour on the original's crashing paths only:** a NULL child to `SetFocusChild` returns after the focus id
  (the original wrote the id through NULL; ComboBox's `SetFocusChild(NULL)` reaches it when the edit box had the
  focus); an empty list with child-only input hits nothing (the original read the list's head as a child); the
  timer set is released in address order at destruction (the original's tree went in its own order).
- **Dialog** (`dialogobj.rs`): the drag, its flags, the Escape result, the default button (held). The drag's two
  `InvalidateRect` calls share one rectangle: `Component::InvalidateRect` moves it by the component's place, so the
  original's second call got the moved rectangle; the Rust passes the same rectangle to both (a fresh one for the
  second fails 1,575 golden sequences). The constructor left `mDragging` unset; it starts false. The status dialog
  saved and restored `mDragging` around its resize (Virtual08 ends a drag): the compiler found it after the move
  (`IsDragging` / `SetDragging`); the census grep had been cut by a `head`. Grep a class's members across all of
  `src` without a limit before moving it.
- **ScrollAreaViewport** is a container with its scroll area (`SetViewportArea`): `InvalidateIfRectVisible` (the
  child's bounds moved up through nested viewports until the scroll area's view) and its `ChildInvalidated` are the
  Rust container's viewport part; `SetCursor` (the area's) and the empty `ChildStateChanged` stay one-line C++
  overrides; its Paint, TimerEvent, SetFocusChild and AddTimerChild were the container's and are gone.
  `ScrollAreaViewport::Reset` had no caller: deleted with the census's `ResetChildren`. ScrollAreaViewport.cpp
  deleted.
- **The goldens** share a world (`tests/won/won_ct_world.h`): twelve components, the first four containers, with
  bounds, flags, parents, timer flags, invalid states, focus ids and control ids, the root, the window's focus, the
  mouse and the cursors. A call the host makes on a component runs what the C++ runs: a container's overrides on
  the side running ("do" lines), and Component's own behaviour for the rest (the focus flag, the invalid state,
  RequestFocus, RequestTimer, Invalidate and AddedToParent calling the parent back, TabFocus); a leaf's answers (a
  key, a tick, CanClose) come from a second random stream. World changes are traced ("set", "env"), pure reads are
  answered from the world. The Rust replay is an interpreter of those lines (no copy of the C++ model): "call" and
  "do" make the calls, "set" and "env" change the world, and every op the Rust makes must be the next "op" line,
  answered by its "=" line.

  | Golden | Sequences | Trace lines | Mutation | Fails |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | container | 20,000 x 40 calls | 12,833,433 | SetFocusChild's modal test dropped | 1,340 |
  | | | | the clip popped unconditionally | 11,122 |
  | container with viewports | 20,000 x 40 calls | 14,208,418 | a nested viewport's rectangle not moved in x | 268 |
  | dialog | 20,000 x 40 calls | 10,321,741 | a fresh rectangle for the second InvalidateRect | 1,575 |
  | | | | MouseDown's button ignored | 12,014 |

  Every reference (children, timer children, cursors, the default button) is given back in every sequence. The
  goldens' first sequences (41 and 44) are replayed by cargo, which fails on a changed line and on a Rust mutation.

  The first viewport driver put the viewport straight under its area, so the nested path's rectangle never
  mattered and its mutation passed: the driver now builds a column viewport inside another (MultiListArea's).
- **Lessons:**
  - Python's `write_text` on Windows writes CRLF: it turned `tools/xbuild.py` and a new test into CRLF files. Edit
    through `read_bytes` / `write_bytes`.
  - cbindgen exports a type only when an exported function reaches it: an enum passed only as an op's integer
    argument (`EeWonCtVirt`, `EeWonCtField`, `EeWonDlgField`) needs cbindgen.toml's `include`.
  - Clippy rejects `1 as *mut c_void` in tests (`manual_dangling_ptr`): `std::ptr::dangling_mut::<c_void>()` is the
    same address 1.
  - The main checkout's oracle ref came from a tree whose `Data/ai` differs: every trace's first line (the AI folder
    hash) differs; the rest is identical (`build/w26/orcmp.sh` compares without it and the timing lines).
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby (the oracle is unchanged by construction; seeds 2-3 identical
  after each commit). Every lobby screen, list, scroll area, button group and dialog is a Container, so the whole
  lobby runs through `ctobj.rs`: the lead's LAN game (`lan_game.py`: the LAN lobby's mouse routing, focus, tab
  order, timers (the caret, the ping), the game room, the join's status dialog) and the lobby captures (paint
  order, clipping, colour schemes, invalidation through the list viewports) are the check. Only a person drags a
  dialog, presses Escape or Enter in one, or tabs through a dialog's controls; those run only in the goldens.
- **Left:** TabCtrl / TabBar, ComboBox (its edit box and button over the container: GetFocusChild and
  GetMouseChild are accessors already), and the older input and list goldens' re-recording to trace the delivered
  event type.

    reference order.
- **The cargo replay is shared.** `ctobj_tests.rs`'s line interpreter takes a golden's own hooks (`Ext`: overrides
  of container calls, pure reads, op lines it prints, top-level lines, cleanup) and a larger world (7 containers,
  24 components). The tab replay is about 150 lines on top of it.
- **Lessons:**
  - cbindgen's renames are global even for a private struct: a helper named `Obj` became `struct
    EeAStarGraphObject;` in ee_won.h (ee_astar's rename) and made ee_astar.h include ee_won.h. Prefix even private
    helper types (`EeWonTabOut`).
  - **Never use `git stash` in these worktrees.** The stash list belongs to the repository, not the worktree. The
    screens lane stashed three seconds before this lane, and this lane's pop then applied the screens lane's stash.
    The work came back from the dangling stash commit (`git fsck --unreachable`, `git stash apply <sha>`).
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby, so the oracle is unchanged by construction (seeds 2-3 identical
  after each commit). The root screen's tab control is built at every lobby entry. The lead's LAN game
  (`lan_game.py`: the LAN tab is selected at entry, the game tab is enabled and selected on joining and the previous
  tab comes back on leaving, through `EnterGameTab` and `GetCurTabId`) and the lobby captures (the tab row, the
  arrows' visibility, the page area's padding) are the check. Keyboard tab switching, tab focus order and the scroll
  arrows (more tabs than fit) run only in the golden unless a person uses them.
- **Left:**
  - ComboBox. Census: only `mShowButtonWhenDisabled` (ComboBoxConfig) needs a setter; `mEdit`, `mButton`,
    `mListBox` and `mListArea` are set and read by MSComboBox, WONComboBox, the skins and the game options control,
    so they stay members, as the tab control's parts did.
  - The move needs about 30 ops: list area, edit box, popup and the undo text (a GUIString member).
  - Then Window/RootContainer, the remaining controls and layout managers, and the input and list goldens'
    re-recording to trace the delivered event type.

## R5b.4, twentieth round: the unit AI scripts and the class improvements in Rust (ee_units script.rs, improve.rs; branch rust-r5b4-core20, 2026-11-13)

| Commit | What | C++ |
|---|---|---|
| e80747d1 | the unit AI scripts whole in Rust (`EEUnitTrigger` deleted; `EEUnitAction` an id view) | +61 -1059, net -998 |
| 67b91082 | objcache: a 0-byte stored object is a miss | (tool) |
| 6cfc2039 | the class improvements' arithmetic in Rust | +120 -443, net -323 |

- **EEUGLocation stays blocked**: combat round 14 is moving `EEUGHealUnit` off it. This round took the next
  biggest self-contained pieces that do not touch the goals: the unit AI scripts and the improvement levels.
- **The scripts: the parser, the model and the name tables.** `Unit AI Scripts\*.tai` are parsed in Rust byte for
  byte as the original (the comment strip, the quote-aware tokens, the `anyof(`/`allof(` lists re-read with `", "`
  after the cursor's rewind, the `true(`/`false(` and `#include("X.tai")` names cut as `UString::Copy` cut them,
  `remove()` skipped, `AddTrigger`'s single-event replacement and removal, the links making empty actions, the idle
  action). Quirks kept: a space after a list's comma ends the whole parse (the empty token stops the loop; no shipped
  script has one), a trigger left open at the file's end is dropped.
- **An action is a Rust object C++ points at.** `EEComplexUnit::mCommand` and `EEUnitClass::FindAction` hand out
  `EEUnitAction*`, and every C++ reader reads only its id: the action is a `#[repr(C)]` Rust struct with the id first,
  and `EEUnitAction` is a view of that one field (`uint32_t mType`). Actions live at stable addresses (`Box`) until
  `DeleteScripts`. The AI step reads the triggers straight from Rust (the host's trigger callback is gone).
- **The name tables were generated, then checked against the headers.** 167 actions and 250 triggers, in the
  registration order, from the deleted `RegisterAll` bodies; a test checks every pair against the enumerators'
  `Register("Name", id)` comments. `std::map::insert` keeps the first registration: two triggers share 12007
  (GarrisonUpgrade first), and the Rust lookup takes the first match.
- **A golden before the C++ went (the golden-driver pattern, in game).** With both parsers in, `GetScript` dumped
  each script both ways (actions, triggers, events, any/all, true/false ids and the linked actions' ids) and compared
  them: identical for all 51 scripts the oracle games load (seeds 2-3). Then the C++ parser was deleted.
- **The improvements: the arithmetic in Rust over two records.** `CanUpgrade`, the base value and the step, the
  integer and float step sums (one f32 addition per step, the truncating casts), a level change and the button's gain
  are Rust (improve.rs) over the class's fields and the upgrade's stats as `#[repr(C)]` records; the C++ writes back
  only the stat a change moved (range with line of sight, through `SetRange`; speed through `SetMaxVelocity`), keeps
  the names (now a table), `Save`, and `Load` with its five version branches folded into one (the same reads in the
  same order). A golden in game compared the original arithmetic (copied, temporarily) with the Rust over every
  class with an improvement table, every improvement, six level changes and their gains: 145,600 checks, 0 different.
  No gate game changes a level (no AI buys an improvement in the oracle games: a temporary print saw none); the
  saveload games load the levels (all at 1).
- **A shared object cache can hand out an empty object.** A link failed on `EEE3DRain.obj` ("unknown file type"):
  the store held a 0-byte object (a truncated write), and every build that hit its key copied it. The lookup now
  treats an empty object as a miss. Two builds of one worktree at once (a background build still writing its layout
  when the next started) interleaved their logs here: wait for a build's notification before the next.
- **Coverage.** Every game parses the scripts its classes name (51 per oracle game) and steps their actions: the
  oracle and the captures gate the scripts. The improvements' arithmetic runs in no gate game (golden and unit tests
  only); its `Load` runs in every saveload game. The scenario editor's action combo box (its names from the Rust

## R4.4, twelfth round: a rasterizer table for Rust draws, and whole effect classes in Rust with their draws (ee_gfx raster.rs, effect_rising.rs, effect_follow.rs; branch rust-gfx18, 2026-11-13)

Round 11 showed the leaf moves returning 10-40 lines a class while the draws stayed C++. This round gives Rust a
way to draw and moves whole effect classes with their draws. Graphics Thread C++ (`src/Empire Earth/Graphics
Thread/*.cpp`): 23,388 lines before the round; 23,127 after the teleport and time warp (-261, net of the new
`EEE3DRust.cpp` and the rasterizer table); 22,651 after the blast wave and shield (-476). Headers: `EEE3DTeleport.h`,
`EEE3DTimeWarp.h`, `EEE3DBlastWave.h`, `EEE3DShield.h` deleted, `EEE3DRust.h` added.

- **The rasterizer as Rust calls it (`raster.rs`).** One C++ table, `gEERustRaster` in `EERenderObject.cpp`, of
  captureless lambdas over `gRasterizer` on the current screen (`gScreenIndex`): alpha reference, fog get and set,
  ambient colour get and set, z buffer, blending, shading colour source, alpha testing, a lighting set-up by kind
  (`ApplyLighting`, round 11's call lists), `GetFogFactor` (which reads the fog's attributes and turns the fog off),
  and a model by handle (`GEModel*`): opacity, post-model transformation, scale, `PrepareTransforms`, `Draw` with
  `gOrthographicView`, material 0's texture, and the texture-coordinate v scroll with its restore (the shield's). Rust
  draws through the `Raster` trait: the table in the game, `LogRaster` in the unit tests. A table of function
  pointers rather than `extern "C"` imports keeps `ee_gfx` free of link-time C++ symbols, so the scratch drivers
  still link `ee_rust.lib` alone. Adding a call is one lambda and one trait method; textures are opaque handles
  from the host.
- **One C++ class for the 3D effects that moved (`EEE3DRust`).** Each virtual (`DrawPass2..6`, `Queue`, `SetUp`,
  `Step`, the constructors on a unit and at a point, `RepairPointers` after `EEEffect`'s, `Load`/`Save` after
  `EEEffect3D`'s) calls `ee_gfx_effect3d` (or `ee_gfx_effect3d_file`) with the op, the record, the graphic effect's
  facts (`EeGfxGraphicFacts`: size, params 1-6, flag 1, duration, alpha reference, the tick, the unit's hit points)
  and the host (`EeGfxEffect3DHost`: the unit's position, the model's height, the region move, the line effects,
  `EEEffect3D::Queue`, the render queue push, the media load, the model, the texture, `FollowUnit`). Rust dispatches
  by the record's kind. The manager makes `EEE3DRust(kind)` where it made the leaf. The record is reached through its
  raw pointer field by field: the host's region move and `FollowUnit` read and write it through the C++ members, so
  no Rust reference to it lives across a host call (rule: no Rust reference across a call back into C++).
- **Moved whole:** the teleport (0x3f) and the time warp (0x44) (`effect_rising.rs`: construction with the two line
  effects, set-up, queue, the depth-mask draw of pass 4, the rise or sink, the media on repair, Load/Save of the
  age), the blast wave (0x18, on a unit or at a point: the additive draw of pass 6 growing or shrinking and dimming,
  the age while aging) and the shield (0x45: the texture scroll between params 2 and 3, the flash on a hit, the fade,
  the draw of pass 5 with its v scroll, Load from before 0.180 and after, Save) (`effect_follow.rs`). New record
  parts: `aged.draw_age`, `aged.location`, `EeGfxEffectShield`. `FollowUnit` (the tag-point geometry) stays the
  host's.
- **Golden drivers over a logging rasterizer** (`build/gx18/rising`, `build/gx18/follow`): the original classes'
  constructors, `SetUp`, `Queue`, draw, `Step` and `FollowUnit` cut verbatim from f839d277 (before rounds 11-12) over
  a stub world (a unit with a complex unit, physical model, tag list or none, a vertex array of 0 to 6 v's, a
  material) and a rasterizer, model and effect manager that print every call; against the new side cut from the

  same bytes: rising 300 effects (5,443 lines) and 3,000 on seed 2 (52,163), follow 300 (6,688) and 3,000 on seed 2
  (67,160). The goldens are not replayed in Rust (the driver's per-call order of LCG draws inside `GEColor(...)`
  arguments is the compiler's); the Rust unit tests pin each op against `LogRaster`.
- **Behaviour:** none intended. The blast wave's, time warp's and teleport's media now come from
  `GetGraphicObject()` everywhere (the time warp and teleport read `mGraphicEffect->mGraphicObject` directly; the

- **Gates.** On the result merged with rust (eb2f738e): `build.py --sim` and the test profile link 0/0, the Rust gate PASS (2,554 tests), the sim oracle identical on seeds 2-7, the captures at seeds 2-3 PASS with EFMU and EFST (oracle 169 digests, late 170, calamity 183); the follow driver rebuilt on the merged tree printed the same bytes. Per commit: the build 0/0; the teleport/time warp commit the oracle at seeds 2-3 identical (its captures were stopped by the disk floor and ran with the next commit's); the blast wave/shield commit the oracle at seeds 2-3 identical, the oracle, calamity and late captures at seeds 2-3 PASS (169, 183, 170 digests), the Rust gate PASS after moving `ffi_effect.rs`'s test module back to the end (clippy). The rising driver was rerun on its own commit, not after the follow commit changed the shared host (its media load now `GetGraphicObject()`, the same object); the follow driver exercises that host. ## R6: WON's Internet code, round 16 (ServerConnection and RoutingConnection's op list and dispatch as Rust objects)

Branch `rust-won-net16`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 15. The servers are gone: only an Internet
login (RoutingLogic::ConnectToServer, EEWonNet's dead server select) makes a ServerConnection or a RoutingConnection,
so no LAN step reaches this round's code; the golden driver and the Rust tests exercise it.

- **Where the socket layer stood.** Round 15's premise ("every remaining Internet class waits on the socket
  objects") was already met: the lobby lane's rounds 14 to 16 made AsyncSocket, SocketOp and its eight ops,
  QueueSocket, LobbyLanSocket, IPAddr, UDPManager and its two ops Rust objects with C++ shims (their state and every
  step; the C++ files left are the shims, the hook tables and the `Winsock numbering` asserts). BlockingSocket has no
  state (each call makes one op and runs it blocking): moving its seven three-line calls would add a hook per op kind
  and delete nothing. SocketThread's two classes were already shims (round 13). So this round went one level up.
- **The golden over real loopback sockets.** `won_servconn_test` (new, `xbuild wontest`): a listener on 127.0.0.1
  and the connection under test, the peer authentication a stand-in that connects the connection's socket for real
  (or stays pending for port 0; PeerAuthOp is a Rust op that needs certificates, so the driver defines PeerAuthOp's
  constructor and RustServerOp's members itself and ServerOp.cpp is not linked). 134 lines for ServerConnection and
  ServerConnectionConnectOp, recorded over the unmodified classes (five runs the same); then 68 for RoutingConnection,
  recorded over its unmodified class (six runs the same), the first 132 lines unchanged (the plain connection's
  deferred destruction now lands at the routing part's first pump). Deterministic by construction: every wait is a
  pump until a completion count (no line depends on the clock but the keep-alive's one-second period, whose
  no-ops are counted, not timed).
- **Driver traps.** WON's message framing counts the length field itself and SendMsg sends the bytes as given: a
  "hello" without its 4-byte length was read as a bad length and closed the connection. RunAsync only queues: a
  ServerConnectionConnectOp run blocking waits on a peer op whose run the pump starts, so it ran 4 s and stayed
  pending (it runs async and pumped). A blocking op on a pending connect races two equal time-outs (the op's and its
  peer op's): left out. A notification cut short is finished in MsgCallback's catch with `status`, a variable no op
  has set yet when the notification's op is first in the list (the golden showed 1150674430): left out of the
  golden; the Rust defines it as `EE_WON_RT_UNPACK_FAILURE` (unit test).
- **ServerConnection** (`servconn.rs`, `EeWonServerConn`): the auth context and type, the peer authentication op, the
  connect completion, the keep-alive timer and its period (a reference each), and every step: StartKeepAlive,
  SetAuth, ConnectCallback (the repeat receive and keep-alive on success), KeepAliveCallback and SendNoOp, the close
  and kill hooks, ConnectAsync and ConnectBlock, under the socket's lock where the C++ held it, references dropped
  where a `SmartPtr` assignment dropped them. A kill may call back into the object (the timer's completion is
  KeepAliveCallback, a pending connect's is the connect completion): no borrow lives across a hook and the slot is
  read again after it. One hook table (19 entries); `ConnectCallback` is no longer virtual (nothing overrode it).
  ServerConnectionConnectOp stays C++ (four short members over the connection; moving it would add more hooks than it
  deletes). Mutation: no keep-alive restart fails the golden from line 59.
- **RoutingConnection** (`routeconn.rs`, `EeWonRouteConn`): the op list, the 61 completions by op type and the
  default one, and AddOp, CalcCompletion, GetUnsolicitedOp, MsgCallback (the header, the new notification op
  first, the walk with the original's dispatch rule, the catch path without the complete hook), CloseHook (an op a
  kill adds is killed too, as the std::list walk did) and KillHook. The completions are set through
  `SetOpCompletion` / `SetDefaultOpCompletion` (EEWonNet and RoutingLogic wrote the array: mechanical, its own
  commit). What stays C++: the request helpers (each makes its C++ op class), the notification ops' constructors
  (one hook with the original's switch), HandleReply over a `ReadBuffer` with its `ReadBufferException` (a flag
  across the C ABI), `mAllDerivedOpsAreUnsolicited` (read by the C++ virtual GetUnsolicitedDerivedOp). A type past
  the 61 slots (the original read past its array) has no completion. Mutation: the type's completion ignored fails the
  golden from line 146. A `c_long` hook return cast to `i32` is a clippy error on Windows (`c_long` is `i32` there)
  and a needed cast on Linux: such hooks return `i32` (`int32_t` in the C++).
- **Net C++** (src+include, the generated headers left out): ServerConnection +100 -117; the completion setters
  +31 -28; RoutingConnection +111 -136; the round +242 -281. Small: each class keeps a hook table (19 and 14
  entries) because its ops, completions and subclasses are still C++.
- **LAN reach: none.** Every LAN lobby and game runs on QueueSocket, LobbyLanSocket, the socket ops and UDPManager
  (the lobby lane's objects, untouched here). ServerConnection and RoutingConnection are made only by an Internet
  login (the WON servers are gone); the lead's LAN gate does not reach this round's code, and neither does EE-SIM.
- **Not moved, and why.** TitleConfig: ConfigObject is still C++ (WONGUI's configs derive from it). The RustServerOp
  host (ServerOp.cpp's HostCall, ServerOp's members): not started this round. SmartRoutingConnection's model,
  commands and snapshots (~1,600 lines) sit on RoutingConnection's request helpers and its own maps: next.

## R6: WON's Internet code, round 17 (SmartRoutingConnection's model, commands and snapshots as one Rust object)

Branch `rust-won-net17`. Measured by net C++ deletion, as rounds 7 to 16. Round 16's net was small because each moved
class kept a hook table while its ops stayed C++; this round took a class whose state and logic are self-contained.

- **What moved.** `smartroute.rs` (`EeWonSmartRoute`): SmartRoutingConnection's client, group and member maps (shared
  records in `Rc<RefCell>`: a member's client is the client map's record, as the original's `SmartPtr`s were, and a
  record dropped from the map lives on in the members and handled slots that hold it), the client, group and member
  iterators and the erase rules that step them, the handled records (`mHandlerClient` / `Group` / `Member`), this
  client's id, record and async flags, the default group, the ignore set (`WStringCompareNoCase` order) and its file
  (read and written through `PlatFOpen` in Rust, `authlogin.rs`'s `read_file` / new `write_file`), the command table
  and settings, the last chat input's error, command, target member and client and matched name. Every step:
  `RoutingOpCompleteHook`'s 25 op types (the merges of client, group and member lists, the joins and leaves, the
  field notifications, the CD key ids from `_KeyId` data objects, the ignored senders whose completion is dropped),
  `HandleInput` / `HandleCommand` (chat.rs's `get_token` / `rest_of_line` / `compare_names` over the CRT's
  `towupper` / `iswspace` / `isalpha` / `atoi`, as the lobby's parser), `FindClient`, `IgnoreClient`, the copies and
  iterators. The C++ class is a shim: it hands each finished op's fields in (`ee_won_smart_put_*` for its lists, then
  `ee_won_smart_op`), and sends the request a chat input returns (`EeWonSmartAction`: chat, flags, invite, moderator,
  mute, ban, ban by CD key) through RoutingConnection's request helpers. No hook table: the Rust object never calls
  back into C++. `SmartRoutingClientInfo` and the `GetNewClientInfo` override are gone (the ops' records are plain
  `RoutingClientInfo`s; nothing outside the model read the smart fields). SmartRoutingConnectionCommands.cpp,
  ...Snapshots.cpp and the three empty units (Events, Models, Sync) are deleted.
- **The API that changed.** Raw records no longer leave the model: `GetGroupMap`, `GetClient(id)` returning a
  `RoutingClientInfoPtr`, `GetMemberRef`, the `Handle*` methods and the public members are gone. EEWonNet (the only
  user) reads copies: `RoutingGroups()` (StartGroupItr / GetNextGroup under the data lock) for the room list, the
  game and room joins and ConnectToLobby's walk; `GetClient(id, ClientInfo&)` in OnChat; `FindClient(name,
  ClientInfo&, bool& found)` and `IgnoreClient(id, on)` for the /ignore and /tell commands; `GetMyClientId()` for
  `mRouting->mClientId`. `GroupInfo` gained `mMemberCount` (the record's +0x2a `mMaxPlayers`, the group list's member
  count), which ListRoomCallback read as the room's maximum players; `GroupInfo::mMaxPlayers` stays the client limit.
  JoinGroupCallback's unused `GetGroup` read is dropped.
- **The golden over real loopback sockets.** `won_smartroute_test` (new, `xbuild wontest`): a SmartRoutingConnection
  connected to a routing server stand-in on 127.0.0.1 that sends the notifications and replies the ops read (built
  from routemsg.rs's formats), recorded over the unmodified C++ class (five runs the same, 668 lines,
  `golden_smartroute.txt`): register with and without the client list (the ignore file read), group and client
  lists merged, joins and leaves, every field notification, chats / invitations / join attempts from an ignored
  client (no completion), the iterators stepped past erased records, a group list removing the member iterator's
  group, the CD key ids, 50 chat inputs with the requests the server receives, the ignore file's bytes, the close.
  The model is dumped after each step: the original's members read directly, the Rust object through
  `ee_won_smart_dump` (the same text; `EE_WON_SMART_ROUTE_RUST` picks the path). Relinked over the shim: 668 lines,
  0 failures, three runs. Mutation: no client-iterator step on an erase fails line 202.
- **Driver traps.** The handled records are reset by every op's hook, so a "sync" notification after each step
  cleared them: they are logged from the default completion, which runs right after the hook for the same op. The
  operands of `+` are unordered: `Log(... + N(c->GetNextMember(m)) + Show(m))` printed the copy before the call.
- **The original's undefined corners, defined.** An iterator a whole-map assignment (register) or clear invalidated
  is at the end; a member without a client is skipped where the original dereferenced it (a leave, a list merge); a
  command whose target is missing names client 0; a non-ASCII duration unit is no letter; `mLastInputCommand` (never
  set by the constructor) starts at 0; `IgnoreClient` by id ignores the record `GetClient(id)` finds (EEWonNet called
  it right after `FindClient` on the same record).
- **Net C++** (src+include, the generated headers left out): +353 -1732 (WONRouting.h +52 -132,
  SmartRoutingConnection.cpp +227 -906, the five deleted units -635, EEWonNet.cpp +74 -59).
- **LAN reach: none.** SmartRoutingConnection is made only by EEWonNet's Internet server select (the WON servers are
  gone); the lobby's RoutingLogic uses a plain RoutingConnection and every LAN game runs on the lobby lane's sockets.
  EE-SIM never makes one. The driver and the Rust tests exercise it.
- **Not moved, and why.** The RustServerOp host (ServerOp.cpp's HostCall, ~600 lines): it answers the Rust ops'
  calls on C++ objects (the socket shims, AuthContext, the GetCertOp objects, files, completions); moving it makes
  every one of those a host call the other way, and the routing ops do not run on it (RoutingConnection drives them),
  so it would not let the routing op classes lose their bodies. The routing request helpers and the notification /
  request op classes (RoutingConnection.cpp, RoutingRequestOps.cpp, RoutingNotifications.cpp): RoutingLogic reads
  their members by class; a move needs the lobby's readers changed with them.

    buttons, the containers and the statics; the default buttons are cleared at the end, so every reference must
    come back.
  - It runs 20,000 sequences with 14,796,987 trace lines, all identical. Five mutations fail it: a radio sibling
    unchecked without its repaint (6,227 sequences), AddedToParent's group walk backwards (6,974), LostFocus
    repainting before giving up the default (4,696), the repeat delay starting at 100 (140), the default's new
    button held before the old one released (3,732); the restored source: 0.
  - `golden_btnobj.txt` holds 41 sequences, replayed by cargo through round 27's `Ext` hooks; the replay fails on
    a button event of another type. The default buttons are process-wide, so the cargo tests that touch them take
    one lock.
- **The input and list goldens** (round 30's second commit): their original sides now fire the original enum and
  both sides trace the type the listeners receive ("fire 20", "fire 22"), as the tab, combo and button goldens do;
  only the fire lines of `golden_inputobj.txt` and `golden_listobj.txt` changed.
- **Lesson:** the mutation run restored the source with `git checkout` before every mutation and finished with an
  unmutated run (0 differing), and nothing was left running (round 29's lesson).
- **What runs it.** EE-SIM never builds the lobby, so the oracle is unchanged by construction (seeds 2-3 identical
  after the commit). Every lobby button runs through `btnobj.rs`: the lead's LAN game (`lan_game.py`: clicking Host,
  Join, Ready, Start and the dialogs' OK buttons, the ButtonPressed events the lobby screens listen for, the
  default button Enter presses in the login and create-game dialogs) and the lobby captures (the pressed, hover,
  checked and default looks the skins paint from `GetButtonFlags`/`IsDefaultButton`/`GetMouseDownState`) are the
  check. Radio groups with arrow keys, Space's hold, repeating arrow buttons held down and a press dragged off a

  over the Graphics and a WrappedText: they need draw ops and only the lobby captures check them, so they were not
  cheap enough for this round. Then Window/WindowManager (platform ops) and the layout managers.
- **The LAN gate's crash on `rust` 37a013f7 (rounds 28-29), fixed here** (its own commit). The host died on the
  MultiPlayer click (a read of NULL + 0x60). The lobby's tab control brings its page to the top in AddedToParent
  (`notify_tab_change`), before the lobby screen joins the root; a page that grabs its background makes the container
  call `GetRootContainer()->AddBG(grabber)` (`CtAddBG`) with a NULL root. The original's AddBG returned before
  reading itself when the grabber had nothing to draw, so the NULL `this` never mattered; since round 29 the
  RootContainer forwarder reads its Rust object first. Container.cpp's host now skips a NULL root (ComponentTraversal
  already did). `lan_game.py` passes again (`RESULT PASS lan-game`).
  - **Why no golden saw it:** the goldens replace the C++ host with their world, and the world traced `CtAddBG` with
    root 0 (env 0) as a harmless op. A method moved behind a forwarder that reads `this->mX` first is no longer
    safe on a NULL `this` that the original's early return tolerated: before moving a class, grep its callers for
    calls through a pointer that may be NULL (`GetRootContainer()->`, `GetRoot()->`).
